Acl.description: A named list of rules evaluated in order; the first match wins.

default_action.description: What happens to IP packets no rule matches; `deny` unless set.

name.description: ACL name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`); the key.

AclAction.description: What a matching rule (or the end of the list) does with the packet.

AclAttachment.description: One device an ACL is installed on.

AclDirection.description: Which way an ACL filters on its device.

AclRule.description:
One match-and-act line of an `Acl`. A field left unset matches anything;
all set fields must match.

action.description: What to do with a packet that matches.

destination.description: Destination prefix, in the same family as `source`.

established.description: Match TCP segments with ACK or RST set (stateless, not connection tracking).

log.description: Log the packets this rule matches.

name.description: Rule name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique within the ACL; the key.

protocol.description: IP protocol to match: `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `icmpv6` or a number; `None` matches any.

source.description: Source prefix; its family limits the rule to IPv4 or IPv6.

AclRuleStatus.description:
One user rule's counters, summed over every filter it compiled to and
every device the ACL is attached to.

action.description: What it does with a match.

dropped.description:
`shadowed` (an earlier rule matches everything it does) or `trailing`
(last rules equal to the default action): the optimiser gave the rule
no filter, so its counters stay 0. `None` when it is installed.

level.description:
The priority level the rule's filters were packed into; `None` when
dropped.

name.description: The rule's name.

AclStatus.description: One ACL: its compile shape, attachments and counters.

attached.description: Every device it is installed on (empty: unattached, counters 0).

default_action.description: What a packet no rule matched gets.

default_bytes.description: Bytes that hit the default action.

default_packets.description: Packets that hit the default action.

filters.description: Kernel filters per attachment, the two default filters included.

levels.description: Priority levels the compiled ACL uses.

name.description: The ACL's name.

AddressFamily.description:
Which NLRI (AFI/SAFI) is exchanged over a peer-group's session —
independent of whatever address family `source_address` resolves to at
runtime, or a peer's `remote_address`. RFC 8950's extended next-hop
encoding allows an IPv6-transport session to carry IPv4 unicast NLRI, so
this must never be derived from, or cross-validated against, either
address's IP version.

Admin.description: The admin section: labelled secrets for other sections to reference.

keys.description: Labelled secrets. Write-only: values print as `<hidden>` everywhere.

label.description: Label other sections reference, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among keys.

secret.description: The secret, 1 to 80 bytes. Write-only: never printed, logged or returned by the REST API.

AsPathList.description:
A named set of AS-path regexes, referenced by bare name from an RPL
script's `this.bgp.as_path in NAME`. Each pattern is matched against the
path rendered as space-separated ASNs, with `_` as the Cisco-style
boundary (see `nos_rpl::AsPathRegexes`); the list matches if ANY pattern
does.

name.description: List name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among AS-path lists.

patterns.description: Regexes over the space-separated ASN path with `_` as boundary; a path matches when any one matches. Never empty.

BfdAuth.description:
RFC 5880 §4.2/§4.3 authentication section: the method picks the
`AuthType`, `key_id` is the wire Auth Key ID.

key.description: Label of the admin key holding the shared secret.

key_id.description: Auth Key ID carried in each packet (RFC 5880 §4.2/§4.3); both ends must agree.

method.description: Mechanism, which fixes the `AuthType` on the wire.

BfdMode.description:
Which BFD a session runs: the classical RFC 5880 handshake, or the RFC
7880 S-BFD initiator (Down/Up only, against a stateless reflector).

BfdProfile.description:
A named set of BFD (RFC 5880) session parameters, referenced by bare name
from a BGP peer-group, an OSPF/OSPFv3 profile or a static route
(`bfd <name>`). Declaration only for now: no daemon consumes it yet, so
attaching one is inert.

oneOf.description:
`None` is RFC 5880 `AuthType` 0: no authentication. The key is a
label of the admin keystore, never an inline secret.

detect_multiplier.description: Detection multiplier (RFC 5880 §6.8.4): detection time is this times the negotiated interval. At least 1.

echo_interval.description:
Echo transmit interval, and the Required Min Echo RX Interval this
system advertises, milliseconds.

minimum_ttl.description: Lowest received IP TTL / Hop Limit a session accepts (RFC 5881 §5 GTSM); lower packets are dropped.

mode.description:
`sbfd`: Seamless BFD initiator (RFC 7880/7881): probes a reflector
that keeps no per-session state. Excludes `echo-mode`, `padded-pdu-size`
and `auth` (not built for S-BFD yet).

name.description: Profile name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among BFD profiles; the key sessions reference.

padded_pdu_size.description:
RFC 9764: pad each Control packet's UDP payload with zeros to this
many bytes, to test that the path carries packets that large. `None`
sends the bare packet.

passive.description:
Passive role: wait for the peer's first packet instead of starting
the session (RFC 5880 §6.1).

sbfd_remote_discriminator.description:
RFC 7880 S-BFD discriminator of the remote entity, written as an IPv4
address (the 32 bits). `None`: the peer's own IPv4 address.

shutdown.description: Administratively down: sessions using this profile stay `AdminDown`.

BfdSessionKind.description:
What a session is: a classical RFC 5880 peer, or an RFC 7880 S-BFD
initiator probing a stateless reflector.

auth_failures.description: Packets dropped by RFC 5880 §6.7 authentication since the session started.

auth_key_id.description: Key ID of the authentication key in use, if the session is authenticated (RFC 5880 section 6.7).

oneOf.description: The configured authentication (never the key), `None` when off.

diag.description: Diagnostic for the last state change.

echo_interval_us.description: Negotiated Echo transmit interval, microseconds; 0 while inactive.

echo_only.description: RFC 9747 unaffiliated Echo: no Control traffic at all.

kind.description: RFC 7880 S-BFD: which end of which protocol this session is.

remote_discriminator.description: Your Discriminator learned from the peer; zero until heard.

tx_pdu_bytes.description: RFC 9764: the UDP payload size Control packets are padded to, 0 when not padded.

BgpAddPath.description:
RFC 7911 ADD-PATH direction for a peer-group's unicast families: whether
this side offers to receive several paths per prefix, send them, or both.
What is actually used per family is negotiated against the peer's own
capability (RFC 7911 §5).

BgpAggregate.description: One aggregate (RFC 4271 §9.2.2.2), keyed by its prefix.

as_set.description:
Carry the contributors' ASNs as an `AS_SET` instead of setting
`ATOMIC_AGGREGATE`.

prefix.description: Aggregate prefix to originate; the key.

summary_only.description:
Withdraw the contributing more-specifics from every peer while the
aggregate is active.

BgpAoKey.description:
One TCP-AO key. `send_id`/`recv_id` identify it on the wire (RFC 5925's
`KeyID`/`RNextKeyID`); `is_current` marks the key a new connection starts
signing with (exactly one key must have this set; on a live session the
peer's `RNextKeyID` decides, RFC 5925 §7.5.2); `is_rnext` optionally asks
the peer to switch to this key next, for rotation without a dropped
session (applied to the live session in place); `exclude_options` (RFC 5925 §5.2, `#[serde(default)]`
so pre-existing on-disk config still loads as today's always-include
behavior) excludes TCP options from this key's MAC coverage — both peers
must agree, or authentication fails.

exclude_options.description: Leave TCP options out of the MAC computation.

is_current.description: Whether this key signs outgoing segments.

is_rnext.description: Whether this key is advertised as the next one to switch to (`RNextKeyID`).

key_ref.description: Label of the admin key holding the master key.

recv_id.description: `RecvID`: the `KeyID` expected in the peer's TCP-AO option.

send_id.description: `SendID`: the `KeyID` this side puts in the TCP-AO option (0 to 255); the list key.

BgpAuth.description:
Transport authentication for a peer-group's sessions — mutually
exclusive mechanisms, matching the kernel (a socket can carry
`TCP_MD5SIG` or TCP-AO keys, never both at once). Keys are labels of
`Config.admin` keystore entries; the secret itself never appears here.

oneOf.description: RFC 2385 TCP MD5 signature — a single shared password.

Md5.description: RFC 2385 TCP MD5 signature — a single shared password.

key_ref.description: Label of the admin key the TCP MD5 signature option is keyed with.

oneOf.description:
RFC 5925 TCP Authentication Option — one or more keys, supporting
rotation via `send_id`/`recv_id` and the `is_current`/`is_rnext`
flags.

Ao.description:
RFC 5925 TCP Authentication Option — one or more keys, supporting
rotation via `send_id`/`recv_id` and the `is_current`/`is_rnext`
flags.

BgpBlackhole.description:
RFC 7999 remotely triggered blackhole: a unicast route from this group's
peers that carries BLACKHOLE (65535:666) and falls inside `prefix_list`
(the authorisation, with normal prefix-list `range` rules: write
`10.0.0.0/8 upto 32` to cover host routes) is tagged `NO_EXPORT` and, once
best, installed as a discard route. It still runs through `import_policy`,
which under the default deny-all must accept it. eBGP peer-groups only.

prefix_list.description: Name of the `PrefixList` bounding which prefixes the peer may blackhole.

BgpConfederation.description:
RFC 5065 §2: the confederation identifier (`None`: not in a
confederation) and the other member ASes (`peers`) — a peer-group whose
`remote_as` is one of them is a confederation-external peer, not an
external one.

identifier.description: AS number the outside world sees for the whole confederation (RFC 5065); `None` means no confederation.

peers.description: AS numbers of the other member sub-ASes, reached over confederation eBGP.

BgpDamping.description:
RFC 2439 route flap damping of routes received from a peer-group, all times
in seconds. A route's penalty rises on each flap, halves every `half_life`,
suppresses the route at `>= suppress` and releases it below `reuse`; it
never exceeds the ceiling implied by `max_suppress`. `Default` is RFC 7196's
conservative recommendation. eBGP peer-groups only (`bgp_instance`).

half_life.description: Seconds for the penalty to halve.

max_suppress.description: Longest time in seconds a route can stay suppressed.

reuse.description: Penalty below which a suppressed route is released again.

suppress.description: Penalty at or above which a route is suppressed.

BgpFlowspecValidation.description:
Knobs of the Flowspec validation procedure (RFC 8955 §6 as updated by
RFC 9117, which is the default).

disable_dest_prefix_rule.description:
Rule (a) of RFC 8955 §6 is not enforced: a flow without a destination
prefix is accepted (the unicast checks (b) and (c) then do not apply).

rfc8955_strict.description:
Validate as RFC 8955 §6 is written instead of RFC 9117: no (b.2)
exemption for flows with an empty or confederation-only `AS_PATH`, and
the eBGP check compares the flow's leftmost AS with the neighbour's.

BgpGracefulRestart.description:
RFC 4724 / RFC 8538 graceful restart of one BGP instance. `Default` is
on, with every timer at its default.

disabled.description:
Turn graceful restart off: no capability is advertised, and no
peer's routes are kept across a reset.

restart_time.description:
Seconds a peer may take to come back before its routes are dropped,
advertised as our own Restart Time (unset: 120, at most 4095).

selection_deferral_time.description:
Seconds a restarting instance waits for its peers' End-of-RIB before
selecting and advertising routes (unset: 360).

stale_time.description:
Seconds a returned peer's kept routes wait for its End-of-RIB
(unset: 180).

BgpInstance.description: One BGP speaker: identity, peer-groups and peers; served by one `nos-bgpd` process.

aggregates.description:
RFC 4271 §9.2.2.2 aggregates this instance originates while some
more specific route is in its Loc-RIB.

asn.description: Local AS number, 1 to 4294967294 (RFC 6793 reserves 0 and 4294967295).

bmp_stations.description:
RFC 7854 BMP stations (collectors) this instance's `nos-bgpd` dials
inside the instance's VRF and exports peer up/down events to.

cluster_id.description:
RFC 4456 route reflector cluster id. `None` resolves to this
instance's own `router_id` — the standard single-RR-per-cluster
convention. Only meaningful when at least one peer-group has
`route_reflector_client` set; harmless (unused) otherwise.

confederation.description:
RFC 5065 confederation: once `identifier` is set, `asn` is this
router's member AS and `identifier` the AS the confederation shows
to the outside. A plain struct (not an `Option`) so the CLI can set
its two fields one at a time. Checked by
`valid_route_reflection_and_server`.

graceful_restart.description:
RFC 4724 graceful restart with RFC 8538's N bit: on unless
`disabled`. While on, a peer that advertised the capability keeps its
routes in use across a session reset, until it sends End-of-RIB or a
timer expires. A plain struct (not an `Option`) so each field can be
set and deleted on its own.

maximum_paths.description:
How many equal paths' next hops a prefix installs in the kernel
(BGP multipath): the best path plus every path tying with it up to
the IGP cost to the next hop and learned from the same neighbouring
AS. Only the best path is advertised. Unset or 1 installs the best
path alone.

name.description: Instance name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among BGP instances.

peer_groups.description: Session templates; their timers are validated together.

peers.description: Neighbors, each naming one entry of `peer_groups`.

redistribute_policy.description:
The name of the RPL policy filtering routes redistributed into this
instance, mirrored from the owning `RoutingTable.redistribute.policy`
(only when `redistribute.to == Bgp`). Derived and read-only, exactly
like `routing_table` above: never set by any `BgpInstanceOp`,
recomputed by `nos-config` (`crate::derive::sync_routing_table_refs`)
on every commit and on load. `nos-bgpd` reads this directly to
resolve its own redistribution policy without scanning every routing
table. Deliberately not rendered by `nos-cli`.

routing_table.description:
The name of the `RoutingTable` that claims this instance (i.e. the
VRF it belongs to), mirrored from that table's `bgp_instance` field.
Derived and read-only: never set by any `BgpInstanceOp`, recomputed
by `nos-config` (`crate::derive::sync_routing_table_refs`) on every
commit and on load, so an operator only ever edits the one
authoritative reference (`RoutingTable.bgp_instance`). `nos-bgpd`
reads this directly to resolve its own VRF without scanning every
routing table. Deliberately not rendered by `nos-cli`.

rpki_caches.description:
RFC 8210 RPKI-to-Router caches this instance's `nos-bgpd` takes its
validated ROA payloads from, reached inside the instance's VRF. One
is used at a time: the lowest `preference` that answers (RFC 8210
§10), ties in list order.

BgpLocalAs.description:
Vendor `local-as` (IOS/Junos; no RFC): the AS this group's peers see
instead of the instance's own (its `asn`, or the confederation
identifier). The OPEN carries `asn`; outbound `AS_PATH` gets `[asn, own]`
(`[asn]` with `replace_as`); a received path gets `asn` prepended unless
`no_prepend`, and holding `asn` counts as a loop for this group's routes.
External (non-confederation eBGP) peer-groups only
(`bgp_instance::valid_route_reflection_and_server`).

asn.description: AS number this group's peers see instead of the instance's own; carried in OPEN.

no_prepend.description: Do not prepend `asn` to the `AS_PATH` of received routes.

BgpMaximumPrefix.description:
Per-address-family maximum-prefix limits; `None` means unlimited. A fixed
struct rather than a list keyed by `AddressFamily`: the family set is
closed, and three fields give the same CLI/REST shape with no enum-keyed
list support in the config path grammar.

oneOf.description: Limit for IPv4 unicast; `None` is unlimited.
Limit for IPv4 Flowspec; `None` is unlimited.
Limit for IPv6 unicast; `None` is unlimited.
Limit for IPv6 Flowspec; `None` is unlimited.
Limit for L2VPN EVPN; `None` is unlimited.
Limit for RT-Constraint membership routes; `None` is unlimited.
Limit for VPN-IPv4; `None` is unlimited.
Limit for VPN-IPv6; `None` is unlimited.

BgpPeer.description:
Associates a remote address with a peer-group, by name — the bulk of
session config (remote-as, source-address, address-families) lives on
the referenced `BgpPeerGroup`, not here.

peer_group.description: Name of the `BgpPeerGroup` that supplies this peer's settings; must exist.

remote_address.description: Neighbor address; the key, unique across every BGP instance.

oneOf.description: Overrides the peer-group's own `shutdown` — see `BgpShutdown`.

BgpPeerGroup.description: Session settings shared by every `BgpPeer` that names this group.

add_path_send_count.description:
RFC 7911: how many paths per prefix this group is sent when ADD-PATH
send is negotiated: the best N by the decision process, after this
group's own filtering (split horizon, export policy). Unset: 2, or
every path for a route-server client. Needs `add_path` send or both.

address_families.description: Families to negotiate; non-empty, no duplicates.

announce_rpki_state.description:
RFC 8097: send each route's RPKI origin validation state to these
peers as a non-transitive extended community, and take the state
from theirs while this instance has no VRP data of its own. iBGP
peer-groups only (`bgp_instance::valid_route_reflection_and_server`).

oneOf.description:
`None` opens sessions with no transport authentication at all.
Keys are admin-keystore labels, never inline secrets — see `BgpAuth`.

bfd.description:
Name of a `BfdProfile` to run BFD with; `None` runs no BFD. Not part
of the session identity: adding or removing it never resets a session.

oneOf.description:
RFC 7999 BLACKHOLE handling for this group's peers; `None` leaves the
community an ordinary one. See `BgpBlackhole`. eBGP only.

RFC 2439 flap damping of routes received from this group; `None`
disables it. See `BgpDamping`.

enforce_first_as.description:
RFC 4271 §6.3 first-AS check: on an eBGP session, an UPDATE whose
`AS_PATH` does not start with the peer's AS is treated as a withdraw.
`None` is on. A `route_server_client` group is always exempt (RFC 7947
§2.2.2.1).

evpn_import_policy.description:
Accept/reject filter for EVPN routes received from this group's
peers (Type-1/2/3/5; Type-4 bypasses it). Unlike `import_policy`,
`None` accepts every EVPN route, so existing deployments keep
working. Rewrites are ignored.

export_policy.description:
Same default-deny semantics as `import_policy`, applied on
advertisement instead of receipt.

flowspec_export_policy.description:
Policy applied to Flowspec rules advertised to this group's peers.
`None` advertises every selected rule.

flowspec_import_policy.description:
Policy applied to valid Flowspec rules received from this group's
peers before best-path selection. Like `evpn_import_policy`, `None`
accepts every rule; rewrites are honoured.

flowspec_validation.description:
RFC 8955 §6 Flowspec validation tuning. Validation itself cannot be
switched off.

graceful_shutdown.description:
RFC 8326 sender side: tag every route exchanged with this group's
eBGP peers with `GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN` (65535:0) and demote what they send
to `LOCAL_PREF` 0, so traffic drains before a `shutdown`. eBGP only
(`bgp_instance::valid_route_reflection_and_server`). Applied live.

graceful_shutdown_receive_disabled.description:
RFC 8326 §4.1 receiver side is on by default (an eBGP path carrying
65535:0 gets `LOCAL_PREF` 0); `true` turns it off. Applied live.

hold_time.description:
`None` defaults to `HOLD_TIME_DEFAULT` (90s). `Some(0)` disables both
the hold timer and keepalives entirely; otherwise must be `>=
HOLD_TIME_FLOOR` (RFC 4271 §6.2). The value actually used by a
session is `min(this, the peer's own proposed hold time)`.

import_policy.description:
`None` defaults to `deny-all` — this NOS never leaves a direction
unfiltered, unlike every other `Option` field on this struct, which
defaults to some permissive/derived behavior. See root `CLAUDE.md`'s
"Default-deny rollout impact".

keepalive_interval.description:
`None` defaults to `negotiated_hold / 3`, computed after negotiation
(RFC 4271's suggested ratio). When both this and `hold_time` are set,
this must be strictly less than `hold_time` — checked one level up,
on `BgpInstance.peer_groups`, since garde's per-field `custom`
closures can't see a sibling field (see `bgp_instance.rs`).

oneOf.description: See `BgpLocalAs`; `None` presents the instance's own AS.

max_hops.description:
RFC 5082 GTSM: the most router hops away the peer may be (1 =
directly connected, 1..=254). Sends with TTL/hop-limit 255 and drops
received packets below `256 - max_hops`. `None` disables it.

maximum_prefix.description:
RFC 4486 §4 per-address-family maximum-prefix limits — see
`BgpPrefixLimit` (`limit 0` = explicitly uncapped). A limit for a family not in `address_families` is
rejected (`valid_peer_group_timers`).

mrai.description:
RFC 4271 §9.2.1.1 `MinRouteAdvertisementInterval`, in seconds: at most
one batch of advertisements per this interval to each peer (withdrawals
are exempt). `None` (or 0) disables pacing — every change is sent at once.

name.description: Group name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique within the instance.

oneOf.description:
`None` defaults to `SelfAddress` for an eBGP peer-group and
`Unchanged` for an iBGP or `route_server_client` one (RFC 7947
§2.2.1) — see `NextHopMode`.

remote_as.description: Expected remote AS, 1 to 4294967294; equal to the local ASN means iBGP.

oneOf.description:
RFC 9234 BGP Role this group's peers are to us — see `BgpRole`. eBGP
only; a change restarts the sessions (it is in the OPEN).

route_reflector_client.description:
RFC 4456 route-reflector client: routes learned from other iBGP
peers are reflected to this peer (and vice versa) instead of being
withheld by the usual iBGP split-horizon rule. Requires this
peer-group's `remote_as` to equal the owning instance's `asn` (an
iBGP peer-group) — checked cross-instance, see
`bgp_instance::valid_route_reflection_and_server`. Mutually exclusive
with `route_server_client`.

route_refresh_stale_time.description:
RFC 7313 §4: seconds routes from a peer stay stale after its `BoRR`
before they're purged as if its `EoRR` had arrived. `None` defaults to
`ROUTE_REFRESH_STALE_TIME_DEFAULT_SECS` (360s); 0 disables the timer.

route_server_client.description:
RFC 7947 route-server client: this peer-group's own ASN is never
prepended to `AS_PATH` when advertising to it, and (via RFC 7911
ADD-PATH) it receives every other route-server-client's path for a
prefix, not just the one instance-wide elected best path. Requires
this peer-group's `remote_as` to differ from the owning instance's
`asn` (an eBGP peer-group). Mutually exclusive with
`route_reflector_client`.

oneOf.description: See `BgpShutdown`. Appended last, like every later-added field.

soft_reconfiguration_inbound.description:
Keep every route received from this group's peers before import
policy, so a policy change is re-evaluated locally without a session
reset or Route Refresh. Costs roughly one extra copy of the peer's
Adj-RIB-In.

oneOf.description: Transport source address, resolved by `nos-bgpd` at runtime; `None` lets the kernel choose.

strict_mode.description:
RFC 9234 §4.2 strict mode: refuse (Role Mismatch) a peer whose OPEN
carries no Role capability. Needs `role`.

BgpPrefixLimit.description:
One address family's RFC 4486 §4 maximum-prefix limit: more than `limit`
accepted (post-import-policy) prefixes from one peer closes the session
with Cease/Maximum Number of Prefixes Reached, unless `warning_only`.
`restart_interval` (seconds) re-allows the session after that long; `0`
keeps the peer down until `clear bgp <instance> <peer>` or a shut/no-shut.

limit.description: Maximum number of prefixes accepted from the peer for the family.

restart_interval.description: Seconds before a session closed for exceeding `limit` restarts; 0 leaves it down.

warning_only.description: Log when the limit is exceeded instead of closing the session.

BgpRole.description:
RFC 9234 §4.1 BGP Role: what this speaker is to the peer. Carried in the
OPEN's Role capability (code 9); the pair must be legal (Provider/Customer,
RS/RS-Client, Peer/Peer) or the session is refused with Role Mismatch.

BgpRouteSummary.description: One IPv4/IPv6 unicast route known to a BGP instance, for `show bgp routes`.

as_path.description: The AS path as text (`65001 65002 {65003,65004}`); empty when local.

best.description: This path is the Loc-RIB best path for the prefix.

next_hop.description: The BGP next hop as received; `None` for a locally redistributed route.

origin_as.description: RFC 6811 origin AS (`None` for a trailing `AS_SET`).

peer.description: The advertising peer; `None` for a locally redistributed route.

BgpSessionState.description:
The FSM state a peer's session is in, as reported by `nos-bgpd`.
`Idle` covers everything before a TCP connection has even reached
`OpenSent` (no active/passive attempt has an OPEN in flight yet) — it is
not a real state in `nos-bgp::fsm`, which only models `OpenSent`/
`OpenConfirm`/`Established`, but is the natural "nothing established yet"
value to report over this protocol.

BgpShutdown.description:
Administrative shutdown (RFC 4486 Cease/Administrative Shutdown). While set
on a peer-group, or on an individual `BgpPeer` (which overrides the group),
no session is opened or accepted; an established one is closed with a
NOTIFICATION carrying `message` as an RFC 9003 shutdown communication.

message.description: Optional RFC 9003 shutdown communication text carried in the NOTIFICATION.

BmpFrameCounts.description: BMP messages sent to one station, by type, since its task started.

end_of_rib.description:
End-of-RIB markers (a Route Monitoring message with no routes), either
stream; not counted in the two fields above.

BmpMonitor.description: The policy view a `bmp-station` monitors (RFC 7854 section 5).

BmpMonitorOut.description:
The Adj-RIB-Out views a `bmp-station` monitors (RFC 8671). Variant order
is the postcard index: `None` first, it is the default.

BmpStation.description: One BMP station (RFC 7854), keyed by its name.

monitor.description:
Which policy view of the Adj-RIB-In the station gets as Route
Monitoring (#864). Appended last: postcard is positional.

monitor_out.description:
Which Adj-RIB-Out views (RFC 8671) the station gets: what NOS sends
to each peer. Default `none`. Appended last: postcard is positional.

name.description: Name of the station; the key.

port.description:
TCP port of the station. Mandatory: BMP has no assigned port, so
there is deliberately no serde default (and `Default` gives 0, which
the commit refuses).

statistics_interval.description:
Seconds between Statistics Reports (RFC 7854 section 4.8); unset =
none (#864). Appended last: postcard is positional.

BroadcastDomain.description:
A named L2 broadcast domain. `SwitchingProfile` references it for L2
membership; `addresses`/`routing_table` independently make the domain's
own bridge device an SVI (switch virtual interface) — a routed L3
attachment point for the domain as a whole, the same flat shape as a
loopback `Interface`'s L3 config (no VLAN/tag concept applies to a
domain's own bridge, so there's nothing for per-tag addressing to buy
it). The bridge device and whatever interfaces are enslaved into it as L2
members are separate Linux links, so there is no conflict between this
and any member's own VRF assignment.

addresses.description: Addresses of the domain's bridge device (SVI); empty for a pure L2 domain.

arp_redistribute.description:
`redistribute from arp to bgp <instance>`: local ARP/ND neighbours on
the domain's bridge are also originated as Type-2 routes carrying the
IP. Must name the same instance as `mac_redistribute`.

connected_redistribute.description:
`redistribute from connected to bgp <instance>`: the domain's own
(SVI) `addresses` are originated as Type-2 routes carrying the
bridge's MAC. Must name the same instance as `mac_redistribute`.

mac_redistribute.description:
`redistribute from mac to bgp <instance>`: the BGP instance this
domain's local MACs are originated into as EVPN Type-2 routes (and
whose received EVPN routes are installed into the domain's FDB).

max_remote_macs.description:
Ceiling on the remote MAC entries `nos-fdbd` installs for this domain
from received EVPN routes; beyond it the lowest MAC addresses win.
`None`: unlimited. Requires a `vni`.

name.description: Domain name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among broadcast domains.

neigh_suppress.description:
ARP/ND suppression: `nos-fdbd` sets `IFLA_BRPORT_NEIGH_SUPPRESS` on the
domain's VXLAN bridge port, so the bridge answers an ARP request or
IPv6 NS itself whenever it holds the target's binding (every remote
Type-2 carrying an IP is installed as one) instead of flooding it
over the fabric. Gratuitous ARP is then no longer flooded to the
VXLAN port either. Off by default; requires a `vni`.

ospf_profile.description:
If set, names an `OspfProfile` this domain's own SVI joins OSPF
under. Requires `routing_table` also set on this same domain — see
`valid_broadcast_domains`.

ospfv3_profile.description:
Same shape as `ospf_profile`, joining `OSPFv3` (RFC 5340) instead — see
`Subinterface.ospfv3_profile`'s doc comment for why this is a
separate field rather than a widened `ospf_profile`.

route_targets_export.description: Route Targets attached to every EVPN route this domain originates.

route_targets_import.description:
Route Targets a received EVPN route must carry (any one) to be
installed into this domain's FDB.

routing_table.description: Routing table (VRF) the bridge device joins, if any.

stp_forward_delay.description: Forward Delay in seconds for this domain's bridge; `None` uses the spanning-tree default.

stp_hello_time.description:
Per-VLAN timers under `mode rapid-pvst`; `None` inherits the global
one. The 802.1Q 13.25 relations are checked on the effective set.

stp_instance.description:
The MST instance (`spanning-tree mst-instance`) this domain's VLAN
belongs to under `mode mstp`. `None`: the CIST. Inert until `nos-stpd`.

stp_max_age.description: Max Age in seconds for this domain's bridge; `None` uses the spanning-tree default.

stp_priority.description:
Per-VLAN bridge priority under `mode rapid-pvst`; `None` inherits
`spanning-tree priority`. A multiple of 4096.

vni.description:
EVPN/VXLAN: the domain's VXLAN Network Identifier. Setting it makes
`nos-watchdogd` run a `nos-fdbd` for this domain. Everything below
requires it — see `valid_broadcast_domains`.

oneOf.description:
The VTEP address (VXLAN local endpoint), resolved at runtime by
`nos-fdbd` over IPC to `nos-interfaced` — never here, like
`BgpPeerGroup.source_address`. `Loopback` means the loopback of the
routing table owning `mac_redistribute`'s BGP instance.

certificate.description: Base64 of the DER client certificate, issued by the REST CA.

lifetime_secs.description: Seconds it is valid for; renew at half of that.

cleared.description:
Always `true`: any maximum-prefix hold is released, and an
Established session was reset with Cease/Administrative Reset.

warnings.description: Non-blocking advice about the committed config; `[]` when none.

CommunityAlias.description:
A named community value (standard/extended/large — inferred from
`value`'s own colon-literal shape, same as an inline literal in a
script), referenced by bare name from an RPL policy script's
`.contains(..)`/`.add(..)`/`.remove(..)` — see root `CLAUDE.md`'s RPL
section.

name.description: Alias name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among aliases.

CommunityGroup.description:
A named, flat set of `community-alias` names and/or inline literals,
referenced by bare name from an RPL script the same way a
`CommunityAlias` is. `.contains(..)` matches if ANY member matches
(standard community-list OR semantics); `.add(..)`/`.remove(..)` apply to
every member. No nesting — a member must be an existing alias name or a
literal, never another group's name (not requested, see root
`CLAUDE.md`'s RPL section).

members.description: Names of the `CommunityAlias` entries in the group; each must exist.

name.description: Group name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among groups.

Config.description: The whole device configuration: each field is one top-level section, and `validate` checks the cross-references between them.

acls.description:
Named, ordered access lists, attached to interfaces with `acl in` /
`acl out`. `serde(default)` so on-disk config saved before this field
existed still loads.

admin.description:
The keystore: secrets under a label, referenced by label from the
sections that need a key. Not shown by `show config` unless asked
(`show config admin`); values never leave the daemons in clear
(logs, REST and `show` print `<hidden>`). `serde(default)` so on-disk
config saved before this field existed still loads.

as_path_lists.description: Named AS-path regex lists that RPL scripts match with `this.bgp.as_path in NAME`.

bfd_profiles.description:
Named BFD parameter sets, referenced by `bfd <name>` from BGP
peer-groups, OSPF/OSPFv3 profiles and static routes. `serde(default)`
so on-disk config saved before this field existed still loads.

bgp_instances.description: BGP speakers; each gets its own `nos-bgpd` process.

broadcast_domains.description: L2 segments that switching profiles and EVPN VNIs refer to.

community_aliases.description: Named community literals that RPL scripts can use by name.

community_groups.description: Named lists of community aliases that RPL scripts can use by name.

hostname.description: System hostname: 1 to 253 characters, hostname charset only.

interfaces.description: Interfaces `nos-interfaced` configures; any interface not listed is left alone.

lldp.description:
System-wide LLDP timers and management address. `serde(default)` so
on-disk config saved before this field existed still loads.

logging.description:
Log export (remote syslog). `serde(default)` so on-disk config saved
before this field existed still loads.

ospf_instances.description: `OSPFv2` speakers; each gets its own `nos-ospfd` process.

ospfv3_instances.description: `OSPFv3` speakers; each gets its own `nos-ospfv3d` process.

policy_definitions.description: RPL scripts that peer-groups reference by name as import/export policy.

port_aggregates.description: Link aggregations of physical ports (static or LACP).

prefix_lists.description: Named prefix lists that RPL scripts match with `this.prefix in NAME`.

routing_tables.description: VRFs; each binds BGP, static, OSPF and `OSPFv3` instances and may pin the REST API.

sbfd_reflector.description:
RFC 7880 S-BFD reflector. `serde(default)` so on-disk config saved
before this field existed still loads.

spanning_tree.description:
Bridge-wide spanning-tree parameters (inert until `nos-stpd`).
`serde(default)` so on-disk config saved before this field existed
still loads.

static_routing_instances.description: Static route sets, each attached to a routing table by name.

stp_port_profiles.description:
Named spanning-tree port settings, referenced by `stp-port-profile`
from interfaces and port aggregates.

switching_profiles.description: VLAN membership profiles an interface attaches with `switching-profile`.

users.description:
Local users allowed to log in. `serde(default)` so on-disk config saved
before this field existed still loads (`nos-configd` then seeds `admin`).

ConfigDiff.description:
The structural difference between two `Config` values. Only what changed
is included — no unchanged section or field is ever present, so a client
can render this directly as a minimal, context-aware diff.

acls.description: Access list changes, including a rule reorder.

admin.description: Field-level, like `lldp`: `Config.admin` is one singleton section (secret values are masked).

oneOf.description: Hostname change, if any.

lldp.description: Field-level: `Config.lldp` is one singleton section, not a keyed list.

logging.description: Field-level, like `lldp`: `Config.logging` is one singleton section.

sbfd_reflector.description: Field-level, like `lldp`: `Config.sbfd_reflector` is one singleton section.

spanning_tree.description: Field-level, like `lldp`: `Config.spanning_tree` is one singleton section.

DfAlgorithm.description:
The RFC 8584 Designated Forwarder election algorithm this PE asks for on
an Ethernet Segment, advertised in its Type-4 route's DF Election extended
community. `Hrw` only takes effect when every PE on the segment advertises
it; otherwise every PE falls back to `Modulo` (RFC 8584 §2.2.3).

DiffStatus.description:
Whether a diffed section is wholly new, wholly gone, or has some fields
changed within it.

EchoMode.description:
Whether this system loops its own Echo packets through the peer (RFC 5880
§6.4). `Affiliated`: the Echo function runs alongside the Control session,
which then slows to one packet a second. `Unaffiliated` (RFC 9747): Echo
is the whole session, for a peer that runs no BFD at all.

cleared.description: The port was err-disabled and is being brought back up.

ErrorBody.description:
The body of every error response: an RFC 9457 problem document.
`instance` is omitted (optional in the RFC; a handler can't see the URI).

detail.description: What went wrong, for this request.

type.description: Always `about:blank`: the status code alone says what kind of problem it is.

EsEntry.description: One locally attached Ethernet Segment, as seen from one broadcast domain.

ad_pes.description:
The PEs whose per-ES Ethernet A-D route for this segment is currently
held (this one excluded): a remote MAC on the segment is only installed
while its PE is listed here.

designated_forwarder.description:
Whether this PE is the segment's Designated Forwarder for the domain's
BUM traffic. A non-DF has flooding to `port` turned off.

df_algorithm.description:
The DF election algorithm in effect (RFC 8584 §2.2.3): `Hrw` only when
every candidate PE asked for it, else `Modulo`.

local_bias.description:
EVPN local bias (RFC 8365 §8.3.1) is fully in place on this segment:
the PE delivers BUM from its own hosts to the segment whatever the DF
role and drops BUM from the other PEs on it. `false` on a single-active
segment (it does not apply) and when the kernel could not be set up
(missing tc modules), in which case only the DF floods to the segment.

pes.description:
Every PE attached to the segment (this one included), in the order the
DF election ranks them.

port.description:
The bridge port the segment attaches through (the bond or its VLAN
sub-link).

single_active.description:
Single-active redundancy: a non-DF blocks the port outright (unicast
too), instead of only refusing BUM.

up.description:
Whether the segment's port is up (carrier). A down segment withdraws its
Type-4 and Type-1 routes and stops being a DF candidate.

EsRedundancy.description:
How the PEs sharing an Ethernet Segment (`PortAggregate.esi`) divide the
traffic (RFC 7432 §8.5): `AllActive` lets every PE forward unicast to the
segment and only the Designated Forwarder flood BUM; `SingleActive` lets
only the Designated Forwarder forward anything, the others' ports being
blocked outright. Announced to the other PEs in the per-ES Ethernet A-D
route's ESI Label community. Only meaningful with an `esi`.

EvpnRouteInfo.description:
What an `Evpn`-sourced candidate is reached through: the remote VTEP (its
one gateway), the remote PE's Router's MAC and the L3 VNI.

vtep.description: Remote VTEP the route is tunnelled to.

EvpnRouteSummary.description:
One received EVPN (RFC 7432) route, for `show bgp evpn`. `route` is the
NLRI rendered by `nos-bgpd` (`[2]:[65000:1]:[<esi>]:[<tag>]:...`) — nothing
downstream interprets it.

local_pref.description: The `LOCAL_PREF` this route is ranked by (0 when RFC 8326 demoted it).

accepted.description: Of those, how many the import policy accepts.

FdbTable.description: A broadcast domain's forwarding table, for `show fdb`.

bridge.description: Bridge and VXLAN device names, once nos-fdbd has resolved/created them.

flood.description: Remote VTEPs BUM traffic is replicated to (one per received Type-3).

neigh_suppress.description:
Whether ARP/ND suppression (`neigh-suppress`) is in effect on the
VXLAN bridge port: the value nos-fdbd last applied to the kernel,
not merely the configured one.

neighbours.description:
IP-to-MAC bindings: local ARP/ND and SVI addresses, and remote Type-2
routes carrying an IP.

segments.description:
The Ethernet Segments this domain is attached to (an aggregate with an
`esi` that is a member of the domain) and this PE's Designated
Forwarder role on each.

vni.description: VXLAN Network Identifier of the domain.

vxlan.description: Name of the VXLAN device, once created.

FieldDiff.description:
One changed (or added/removed) field — either a top-level scalar or one
field within a `SectionDiff`. Values are pre-formatted strings; the
client only needs to display them, never interpret them.

new.description: `None` only when the field's owning section is being `Removed`.

old.description: `None` only when the field's owning section is newly `Added`.

FlowspecRouteSummary.description:
One received Flowspec (RFC 8955) route, for `show bgp flowspec`. `nlri` is
the component list rendered by `nos-bgpd`; nothing downstream interprets it.

actions.description:
The traffic actions decoded from the extended communities, one text
each (`discard`, `redirect rt 65000:10`, `dscp 10`); a traffic-rate
shadowed by an earlier one is suffixed `(ignored)`.

dataplane.description:
For the selected copy of a rule only, its state in `nos-acld`:
`installed`, `unsupported (<why>)`, `not-attached` (no `flowspec`
device in this instance's table) or `unknown` (`nos-acld` did not
answer); `None` for any other copy.

nlri.description: The NLRI rendered as text (`dest 192.0.2.0/24 proto =6 dst-port =25`).

FlowspecRuleStatus.description:
One flow rule's state in the dataplane, for `show acl` and
`GET /v1/flowspec`.

bytes.description: Bytes matched, summed over every device.

instance.description: The BGP instance that pushed it.

packets.description: Packets matched, summed over every device.

unsupported.description:
Why it is not installed (an unsupported match or action, the rule
cap); `None` when installed.

GrSummary.description: A peer's RFC 4724 / RFC 8538 graceful restart capability.

families.description: The families it keeps forwarding state for, and each one's F bit.

prefixItems.description:
Which NLRI (AFI/SAFI) is exchanged over a peer-group's session —
independent of whatever address family `source_address` resolves to at
runtime, or a peer's `remote_address`. RFC 8950's extended next-hop
encoding allows an IPv6-transport session to carry IPv4 unicast NLRI, so
this must never be derived from, or cross-validated against, either
address's IP version.

notification.description: RFC 8538 N bit: a NOTIFICATION other than a Hard Reset keeps routes.

restarting.description: R bit: the peer has just restarted.

Interface.description:
A named network interface. For a loopback interface (see
`LOOPBACK_PREFIX`), `addresses`/`routing_table` carry its (flat) L3
config directly, exactly as before this type gained subinterfaces — a
loopback has no VLAN/dot1q concept, so there's nothing for per-tag
addressing to buy it. For every other (physical) interface, `addresses`
must be empty and `routing_table` must be unset: all of its L3 config
lives under `subinterfaces` instead, tag 0 for the untagged/native case
(what used to be these same flat fields) — see `valid_addressing_split`.

`switching_profile`, if set, names a `SwitchingProfile` trunking this
interface into one or more `BroadcastDomain`s — unchanged, still a
physical-interface-level field regardless of `subinterfaces`. A tag
claimed by an L2 `switching_profile` member and a tag claimed by an L3
`Subinterface` are mutually exclusive on the same interface: Linux only
allows one master device per link (physical or per-tag sub-link), and an
L2 member wants that link's master to be the domain's bridge while an L3
subinterface wants it to be a VRF. See
`valid_subinterface_and_switching_profile_tags`, wired one level up on
`Config.interfaces` (`valid_interfaces`) since it needs to see sibling
fields — the same reason `RoutingTable`'s redistribute rule is wired on
`Config.routing_tables`.

acl_in.description:
Names an `Acl` filtering IP packets arriving on this link; the placement
rules are `acl::valid_acl_references`.

acl_out.description: Names an `Acl` filtering IP packets leaving this link.

addresses.description: Addresses on the link itself (the loopback case); a physical interface carries L3 config on subinterfaces.

flowspec.description:
Applies the flowspec rules of the BGP instance owning this device's
routing table to the IP packets arriving here (RFC 8955 section 5:
ingress only); placement rules are `acl::valid_flowspec_placements`.

lacp_port_priority.description:
The LACP Actor Port Priority `nos-lacpd` advertises for this link
(802.1AX); `None` = 32768. Lower is higher priority. Only meaningful
while `port_aggregate` names a `Lacp`-mode aggregate; ignored (not
rejected) otherwise.

lldp_destination.description:
Which 802.1AB destination group this link's LLDPDUs use. Both ends
must agree. Physical interfaces only — see `valid_lldp_physical_only`.

lldp_receive.description:
Whether `nos-lldpd` receives and records neighbors' LLDPDUs on this
link. Independent of `lldp_transmit`.

lldp_transmit.description:
Whether `nos-lldpd` transmits LLDPDUs (IEEE 802.1AB) on this link.
Physical interfaces only — see `valid_lldp_physical_only`. `serde(default)`
so on-disk config saved before this field existed still loads.

mtu.description:
The link's MTU, in bytes. A link-layer property of the physical (or
loopback) interface itself — unlike `addresses`/`routing_table`, it's
not part of the loopback/physical addressing split (see
`valid_addressing_split`): a VLAN `Subinterface` follows this
value unless it sets its own (smaller) `mtu`. `None` leaves whatever MTU the
kernel link already has untouched (`nos-interfaced`'s Linux driver
never resets it to a default) rather than forcing 1500.

name.description: Kernel interface name; `loopback-<table>` is a routing table's loopback.

ospf_profile.description:
If set, names an `OspfProfile` this loopback interface joins OSPF
under. Requires `routing_table` also set — see
`valid_addressing_split`. Unused (must be unset) on a physical
interface — its OSPF attachment lives on a `Subinterface` instead,
like `routing_table`.

ospfv3_profile.description:
Same shape as `ospf_profile`, joining `OSPFv3` (RFC 5340) instead — see
`Subinterface.ospfv3_profile`'s doc comment for why this is a
separate field rather than a widened `ospf_profile`.

port_aggregate.description:
If set, names a `PortAggregate` this interface is a static bonded
member of. Mutually exclusive with `switching_profile` and a non-empty
`subinterfaces` — a bonded slave, like a VRF- or bridge-enslaved link,
can only have one Linux master device. See
`valid_port_aggregate_membership`.

routing_table.description: Routing table (VRF) the link joins, if any.

stp_port_profile.description:
Names an `StpPortProfile` for this link as a spanning-tree port. Inert
until `nos-stpd`; refused on a bond member (the STP port is the bond).

subinterfaces.description: L3 attachment points of a physical interface, one per VLAN tag.

switching_profile.description: `SwitchingProfile` that makes this interface an L2 switch port.

InterfaceAddress.description:
One address on an interface, with an optional label. The label is
stored from commit time onward but not yet applied to the kernel by any
driver (no `ip addr ... label` call) — schema/plumbing only for now.

address.description: Address with prefix length, e.g. `192.0.2.1/24`; the key.

label.description: Optional label to pick this address by, e.g. from a BGP source address; not yet applied to the kernel.

InterfaceStatus.description:
One interface's current desired state, as reconciled by `nos-interfaced`
from the running config. This reflects *desired* state — `nos-interfaced`
does not yet apply it to the OS (see `interface/CLAUDE.md`), so it is not
necessarily what the kernel actually has configured.

`addresses`/`routing_table` are populated only for a loopback interface
(flat L3 config, unchanged); every other interface's L3 config lives in
`subinterfaces` instead — see `schema::Subinterface`.

err_disabled.description:
Observed: held administratively down by `nos-stpd`'s BPDU guard
(err-disabled). Read back by a restarting `nos-stpd`.

link_local_address.description:
This interface's kernel-assigned IPv6 link-local address (`fe80::/10`
scope), if the Linux driver has observed one — `None` until the
kernel auto-assigns it (or under the `noop` driver, always). Unlike
every other field here, this reflects **observed kernel state**, not
desired config: `nos-interfaced` never writes a link-local address
itself (see `interface/CLAUDE.md`'s "never touch kernel-auto-assigned
addresses" note) — it only surfaces what the kernel already assigned,
purely so a consumer like `nos-ospfv3d` can source real RFC 5340
Hello/Link-LSA traffic from it without its own kernel access.

mtu.description:
This interface's configured MTU, or `1500` (Linux's own default) if
unset — reflects desired config like every other field here, is
the default for every one of `subinterfaces`, each of which may
override it (`SubinterfaceStatus.mtu`).

name.description: Interface name.

port_aggregate.description:
If set, names the `PortAggregate` this interface is a static bonded
member of — same shape/role as `switching_profile`.

routing_table.description: Routing table (VRF) the object is enslaved to, if any.

LacpMode.description:
A member port's 802.1AX `LACP_Activity`: `Active` ports send LACPDUs
whenever the link is up; `Passive` ones stay silent until they hear an
`Active` partner (two `Passive` ends never form a bundle).

LacpMuxState.description:
802.1AX §6.4.15 Mux Machine states. `Distributing` is the only state in
which this port belongs in the aggregate's active-member set pushed to
`nos-interfaced` (`nos_proto::interface::LacpAggregateMembers`).

LacpPortStatus.description: One member port's current LACP state, for `show lacp`.

actor_churn.description:
802.1AX §6.4.17: this port's own side has been out of sync for a whole
churn-detection time. A churned port is kept out of the bond.

actor_port_priority.description: This port's advertised Actor Port Priority.

individual.description:
The partner's last LACPDU had `Actor_State.Aggregation` clear: it
treats this link as an Individual (non-aggregatable) one, so the port
is never selected into the bond.

partner_churn.description: Same, for the partner's advertised state.

partner_key.description: Partner Operational Key; the administrative default (1) while defaulted.

partner_port_number.description: Partner Port number; the administrative default (1) while defaulted.

partner_port_priority.description: Partner Port Priority; the administrative default (0xff) while defaulted.

partner_system_id.description:
The partner's system id as last heard; the administrative default
(system all-zero, key 1, port 1, priorities 0xffff/0xff, as Linux
`bond_3ad.c`) while `Defaulted` or before any LACPDU was received.
Kept (not reset) while `Expired`.

partner_system_priority.description: Partner System Priority; the administrative default (0xffff) while defaulted.

selected.description:
This port's Selection Logic outcome (`selection.rs`) — `true` iff it
agrees with the aggregate's other `Current` ports on partner
identity.

synchronized.description:
The partner's advertised Synchronization bit on its most recent
LACPDU.

unsupported_version_pdus.description:
LACPDUs dropped because their Version byte was neither 1 nor 2. In
memory only: restarts at 0 with the port's link task. Last field:
postcard is positional (daemons and CLI ship together).

LacpRate.description:
How often this end asks its LACP partner to send LACPDUs (802.1AX's
`LACP_Timeout`), and therefore how long it waits before declaring the
partner gone: `Slow` is every 30s (90s to detect loss), `Fast` every 1s
(3s to detect loss). Only meaningful for a `Lacp`-mode aggregate. Like
Linux bonding's `lacp_rate`, it's a request to the partner — each end
transmits at the rate the *other* end asks for.

LinkInterfaceState.description:
RFC 2328 §9.1's interface states, as they apply to this phase's Hello-only
scope: `PointToPoint` is fixed forever on a point-to-point link (no
election ever runs); a broadcast link starts `Waiting`, then becomes
`Dr`/`Backup`/`DrOther` once RFC 2328 §9.4 election runs (see
`ospf::election`).

LinkType.description: The link type for the RSTP rapid transitions (`AdminPointToPointMAC`).

LldpDestination.description:
Which 802.1AB destination group an interface's LLDPDUs use. Both ends of a
link must agree: a frame to a different group is never seen.

LldpLinkAggregation.description: A neighbor port's link aggregation state.

enabled.description: The port is in an aggregation now.

port_id.description:
The aggregated port id (the sender's aggregate ifIndex), 0 when not
aggregated.

LldpLinkStats.description:
One LLDP-enabled interface's IEEE 802.1AB §9.2.6 statistics (the
LLDP-MIB `lldpStatsTxPortTable`/`lldpStatsRxPortTable` counters), for
`show lldp statistics`. Every counter resets only when `nos-lldpd`
restarts or LLDP is turned off on that interface.

ageouts.description: `statsAgeoutsTotal`: neighbors dropped because their TTL lapsed.

frames_discarded.description:
`statsFramesDiscardedTotal`: every invalid frame, plus every frame
dropped because the neighbor table was full.

frames_in.description:
`statsFramesInTotal`: valid LLDPDUs received (our own reflected frames
excluded).

tlvs_discarded.description:
`statsTLVsDiscardedTotal`: optional TLVs dropped (a malformed or non-IP
Management Address, or one past the per-LLDPDU cap; a malformed or
repeated 802.1/802.3 TLV nos decodes, or a VLAN Name past the cap).

tlvs_unrecognized.description:
`statsTLVsUnrecognizedTotal`: reserved TLV types and every
organizationally-specific TLV nos doesn't decode (LLDP-MED, DCBX, …).

too_many_neighbors.description:
New neighbors refused because the table was full (802.1AB
tooManyNeighbors; this port's share of `lldpStatsRemTablesDrops`).

LldpMacPhy.description: A neighbor port's IEEE 802.3 auto-negotiation and MAU type.

LldpNeighbor.description:
One remote system heard on one local interface, for `show lldp neighbors`.

Chassis/Port IDs are already formatted for display by `nos-lldpd` (a MAC
subtype as `aa:bb:..`, an interface-name subtype as its text, anything
else as hex) — this type is deliberately not a faithful copy of the
802.1AB subtype/value pair, since nothing downstream needs to interpret it.

capabilities.description: The capabilities the neighbor has *enabled*, by name (e.g. `router`).

oneOf.description: IEEE 802.1 (or the deprecated 802.3) Link Aggregation TLV.

local_interface.description: Local port the neighbor was heard on.

oneOf.description: IEEE 802.3 MAC/PHY Configuration/Status TLV.

management_addresses.description: Management addresses the neighbor advertised (already formatted).

max_frame_size.description: IEEE 802.3 Maximum Frame Size, in bytes.

port_vlan_id.description: IEEE 802.1 Port VLAN ID (0: the port has none).

ttl_remaining_secs.description: Seconds until this entry ages out, unless refreshed first.

vlan_names.description: IEEE 802.1 VLAN Name TLVs, in the order received.

LldpSettings.description: System-wide LLDP settings. `None` for a timer means the 802.1AB default.

management_addresses.description:
Each advertised in its own Management Address TLV on every
LLDP-enabled link (at most 4). Taken as configured: an address on a
kernel interface carries that interface's ifIndex, any other is still
sent, with the interface numbering "unknown".

system_description.description: The System Description TLV text; `None` advertises `nos`.

tx_hold.description: `msgTxHold`: the advertised TTL is this × the interval.

LldpVlanName.description: One VLAN a neighbor's port carries, with its name.

name.description: VLAN name.

LogEntry.description:
One structured log record, as forwarded by any component process to
`nos-logd` (`LogRequest::Push`) or returned to a querying client
(`LogEvent::Logs`/`Line`).

fields.description:
The event's structured fields (other than `message`), flattened to
their `Display`/`Debug` text — e.g. `("table", "rt1")`.

message.description: The message text, including structured fields.

source.description:
Identifies which process emitted this entry, e.g. `"nos-ribd[rt1]"`,
`"nos-bgpd[r1]"`, `"nos-interfaced"`, `"nos-configd"`,
`"nos-watchdogd"` — the same identity `nos-watchdogd` already uses
for its own `ProcessSpec` names.

target.description: The `tracing` event's target (typically a module path).

timestamp_ms.description:
Milliseconds since the Unix epoch, from the forwarding process's own
clock — `nos-logd` never rewrites this on receipt, so ordering
reflects when the event was emitted, not when it arrived.

LogLevel.description:
Wire twin of `tracing::Level` — kept separate so no component needs to
depend on `tracing`'s own (de)serialization support.

syslog.description: Remote syslog collectors every log entry is exported to.

csr.description: Base64 of a DER PKCS#10 certificate request for an ECDSA P-256 key you generated.

MacEntry.description: One MAC in a domain's forwarding table.

esi.description: The Ethernet Segment a `Local` MAC was learned on, when its port is one.

vtep.description: The remote VTEP for a `Remote` entry (the first of `vteps`).

vteps.description:
Every VTEP a `Remote` entry is reached through: one, or several when
the MAC sits on an all-active Ethernet Segment and traffic is balanced
over its PEs (aliasing, RFC 7432 §8.4.1.1). Empty for a `Local` MAC.

MacSource.description: How a MAC or neighbor entry was learned.

MstInstance.description: One MST instance and this bridge's priority in it.

priority.description: Bridge priority in this instance, a multiple of 4096.

NeighEntry.description: One IP-to-MAC neighbor entry of an IP-VRF.

vtep.description: The remote VTEP for a `Remote` entry.

NetworkType.description:
Which RFC 2328 network type an attach point using this profile runs.
`OspfProfile.network_type` is `Option` — see its doc comment for how an
unset value is resolved.

NextHopMode.description:
Controls the `NEXT_HOP` path attribute this instance writes into every
UPDATE it advertises to a peer-group's sessions. `SelfAddress` rewrites it
to the session's own local address ("next-hop-self"); `Unchanged`
preserves the next-hop the route already carries (the address it was
received with, for a peer-learned route). `BgpPeerGroup.next_hop: None`
resolves to `SelfAddress` for an eBGP peer-group and `Unchanged` for an
iBGP or route-server-client one — standard BGP practice, since an iBGP speaker must not silently
mask a route's real eBGP-learned next-hop unless explicitly told to.

OspfArea.description:
One OSPF area within an `OspfInstance`, keyed by its dotted-quad area id
(e.g. `0.0.0.0` for the backbone). Unique only within its owning
instance — never referenced from outside `OspfInstance`, unlike
`OspfProfile.name` — so uniqueness is enforced on the parent's `areas`
field (`ospf_instance::unique_area_ids`), not here.

area_id.description: Area id in dotted-quad form; 0.0.0.0 is the backbone.

area_type.description:
RFC 2328 §3.6 stub area (no AS-external LSAs, E-bit clear) or
totally stubby (an ABR also sends no Type-3 but its default), or an
RFC 3101 NSSA (no Type-5, but its own ASBRs' Type-7s, translated into
Type-5s by one ABR). Every router on the area's links must agree, or
their Hellos are dropped. The backbone (`0.0.0.0`) can't be either.
Checked with its siblings by `valid_area_settings`, one level up.

nssa_default_originate.description:
RFC 3101 §2.7: as an ABR of this NSSA, originate a default Type-7
(P-bit clear, so never translated) into it. NSSA only.

nssa_translate_always.description:
RFC 3101 `NSSATranslatorRole` `Always`: as an ABR of this NSSA, always
translate its Type-7s into Type-5s (and set the Router-LSA Nt-bit),
instead of only when elected (`Candidate`, the default). NSSA only.

profiles.description: Interface profiles declared in this area, referenced by an interface's `ospf` attachment.

ranges.description:
RFC 2328 §3.5 address ranges, applied by an ABR to this area's own
intra-area prefixes when summarizing them into its other areas: every
covered prefix is suppressed, and an advertised range with at least
one active component is sent as one Type-3 (metric = the largest
component cost) and installed as a discard route on the ABR.

stub_default_cost.description:
The cost of the default an ABR originates into this stub area or NSSA
(RFC 2328 `StubDefaultCost`). `None` means 1; only allowed on a stub
area or NSSA.

virtual_links.description:
RFC 2328 §15 virtual links whose transit area is this one, keyed by
the far endpoint's router id: a backbone adjacency tunnelled across
this area to a router that is also attached to area 0.0.0.0, joining
a partitioned or detached backbone. Not allowed on the backbone or on
a stub area or NSSA. Up while the endpoint is reachable in this area.

OspfAreaRange.description: One RFC 2328 §3.5 area address range, keyed by `cidr`.

cidr.description: The summarised address range; the key.

not_advertise.description:
RFC 2328's `DoNotAdvertise`: the covered prefixes are hidden from the
other areas entirely. `false` (the default) advertises the range.

OspfAreaType.description: What kind of RFC 2328 area an `OspfArea` is.

OspfAuth.description:
A profile's own authentication — RFC 2328 Appendix D. Mutually exclusive
mechanisms, mirroring `BgpAuth`'s exact shape (`schema::bgp_peer_group`).
Keys are labels of `Config.admin` keystore entries, never inline secrets.
`OspfProfile.auth == None` is RFC 2328's `AuType` 0 (Null) — no separate variant needed for it.

oneOf.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix D.2 — a single up-to-8-byte plaintext password,
carried directly in the OSPF header's 8-byte Authentication field.

Simple.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix D.2 — a single up-to-8-byte plaintext password,
carried directly in the OSPF header's 8-byte Authentication field.

key.description: Label of the admin key holding the password (at most 8 bytes).

oneOf.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix D.3 / RFC 5709 — one or more keys, supporting
rotation via `key_id`/`is_current`, mirroring `BgpAoKey`.

Crypto.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix D.3 / RFC 5709 — one or more keys, supporting
rotation via `key_id`/`is_current`, mirroring `BgpAoKey`.

keys.description: The keychain; `is_current` selects the signing key, the rest allow rotation.

OspfCryptoAlgorithm.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix D's original Cryptographic authentication (plain MD5)
plus RFC 5709's HMAC-SHA extension. The wire's `AuType` is `2` for all
five — there's no separate "algorithm" field on the wire, so `key_id`
alone must unambiguously determine which algorithm a receiver uses.

OspfCryptoKey.description:
One cryptographic auth key, shared by `OspfProfile.auth` (RFC 2328 D.3)
and `Ospfv3Profile.auth` (RFC 7166). `key_id` is the wire Key ID — 16
bits, RFC 7166's Security Association ID width; RFC 7474's `AuType` 3 Key
ID is 32 bits, but RFC 2328's classic `AuType` 2 field is one octet, so
`valid_profile_timers` caps a non-extended `OSPFv2` key at 255 (the type
itself doesn't). `is_current` marks the key actively signing outgoing
packets (exactly one key must have this set) — every configured key is
still accepted on receive, looked up by the wire's own Key ID (RFC 2328
D.5), which is how graceful key rollover works without dropping the
adjacency.

is_current.description: Whether this key signs outgoing packets.

key.description: Label of the admin key holding the shared secret.

key_id.description: Key id carried in the authentication trailer; the list key.

OspfInstance.description:
A named OSPF instance. Basic configuration only today — `router_id`, the
routing-table (VRF) association mirroring `BgpInstance`'s own minimal
shape, and `areas` (dotted-quad-keyed, see `OspfArea`). No interfaces
beyond what a nested area's profiles can be attached to yet, and no wire
protocol — this is a config-only skeleton, see `docs/protocols/ospf-internals.md`.

areas.description: This instance's OSPF areas, keyed by `area_id` — see `OspfArea`.

graceful_restart_grace_period.description:
RFC 3623 graceful restart: on a planned shutdown, send a Grace-LSA
asking every `Full` neighbor to keep the adjacency (and this router's
routes) for this many seconds while the daemon restarts. `None`
(default) disables it. Helper mode needs no config — every instance
always helps a restarting neighbor.

host_router.description:
RFC 8770 host router: sets the H-bit in this router's Router-LSA so
the rest of the area never routes transit traffic through it, and
advertises its transit links at 65535 for routers that don't honour
the bit. Its own prefixes stay reachable. Refused with a
`redistribute … to ospf` rule on its routing table (a host router is
no ASBR). Off by default.

max_metric_administrative.description:
RFC 6987 stub router until turned off — drains transit traffic before
maintenance. Off by default.

max_metric_on_shutdown.description:
RFC 6987 stub router for this many seconds (1-3) when `nos-ospfd`
stops (not on a graceful restart), before it withdraws its LSAs, so
traffic moves away first. At most 3s: that plus the 6s withdrawal fits
`nos-watchdogd`'s 10s stop budget. `None` (default) disables it.

max_metric_on_startup.description:
RFC 6987 stub router for this many seconds (5-86400) after
`nos-ospfd` starts: every transit link in its Router-LSA costs 65535,
so traffic avoids the router while its routes converge; its own
prefixes stay reachable. Takes effect on the next start, and is
skipped after an RFC 3623 graceful restart. `None` (default) disables
it, and ends a period that is still running.

name.description: Instance name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among `OSPFv2` instances.

prefix_suppression.description:
RFC 6860 prefix suppression: hide transit-only networks. Leaves every
point-to-point link's subnet out of this router's Router-LSA and gives
the Network-LSA it originates as DR a /32 mask, so other routers
install no route to them. Loopbacks stay advertised. Off by default;
`#[serde(default)]` so configs saved before this field existed still
load.

redistribute_metric.description:
`RoutingTable.redistribute.metric` mirrored like `redistribute_policy`
(derived, read-only, hidden): the external metric `nos-ospfd` puts in
the Type-5/Type-7 LSAs it originates (`None` = 20).

redistribute_policy.description:
The name of the RPL policy filtering routes redistributed into this
instance, mirrored from the owning `RoutingTable.redistribute.policy`
(only when `redistribute.to == Ospf`). Derived and read-only, exactly
like `routing_table` above: never set by any `OspfInstanceOp`,
recomputed by `nos-config` (`crate::derive::sync_routing_table_refs`)
on every commit and on load. `nos-ospfd` reads this directly to
resolve its own redistribution policy without scanning every routing
table. Deliberately not rendered by `nos-cli`.

remote_lfa.description:
RFC 7490 remote loop-free alternates: for a destination with no basic
LFA, a backup that tunnels (IP-in-IP) to a PQ node's loopback. Also
makes this router's routing table decapsulate IP-in-IP from any
source, so it can be another router's PQ node — enable it on every
router of the area. Off by default.

router_id.description: OSPF router id (RFC 2328 §C.1), written as a dotted-quad.

routing_table.description:
The name of the `RoutingTable` that claims this instance (i.e. the
VRF it belongs to), mirrored from that table's `ospf_instance` field.
Derived and read-only: never set by any `OspfInstanceOp`, recomputed
by `nos-config` (`crate::derive::sync_routing_table_refs`) on every
commit and on load, so an operator only ever edits the one
authoritative reference (`RoutingTable.ospf_instance`). `nos-ospfd`
reads this directly to resolve its own VRF without scanning every
routing table. Deliberately not rendered by `nos-cli`.

OspfNeighborState.description:
One neighbor's state, as reported by `nos-ospfd` — the full RFC 2328
§10.5 ladder. `Down` is an ongoing, valid state (no Hello received yet,
or the dead-interval expired) — a point-to-point link always reports at
least one row, even `Down`; a broadcast link reports one row per
currently-known neighbor (zero if none yet — there's no single fixed peer
to show a placeholder for on a multi-access segment).

OspfProfile.description:
A named OSPF profile, declared inside an area (`OspfArea.profiles`) but
referenced by bare name from any L3 attach point's `ospf_profile` field
(`Interface`/`Subinterface`/`BroadcastDomain`) with no instance/area
qualifier — so, like `BgpPeerGroup.name`, its uniqueness is enforced
globally across the whole config, not just within its owning area.

oneOf.description: `None` is RFC 2328 `AuType` 0 (Null) — no authentication.

bfd.description:
Name of a `BfdProfile` to run BFD with; `None` runs no BFD.
Inert until `nos-bfdd` exists.

cost.description:
Interface cost, in the usual OSPF sense (lower is preferred by
SPF). `None` defaults to `1` — a real behavioral consumer:
`ospf::link::originate::router_lsa_links`/`originate_router_lsas` use it as
this link's RFC 2328 §16 metric, and `ospf::spf::compute` sums it
along the Dijkstra path. `0` is rejected (not a valid OSPF cost).

dead_interval.description:
`None` defaults to `DEAD_INTERVAL_DEFAULT` (40s). When both this and
`hello_interval` are set, this must be strictly greater than
`hello_interval` — checked one level up, on `OspfArea.profiles`,
since garde's per-field `custom` closures can't see a sibling field
(see `ospf_area.rs`, mirrors `bgp_peer_group`'s identical
hold-time/keepalive-interval pattern).

extended_sequence_numbers.description:
RFC 7474: sign with `AuType` 3 — a 64-bit (persisted boot count :
counter) sequence number and a digest bound to the IP source address —
closing the replay window across router restarts. Only valid with
`Crypto` auth using HMAC-SHA keys (no MD5); both ends of a link must
agree, since `AuType` 3 and 2 don't interoperate. Checked one level
up in `valid_profile_timers`, since it needs the sibling `auth`.

mtu.description:
`None` resolves to the attach point's own real interface MTU (queried
from `nos-interfaced`), falling back to 1500 if unavailable.
Overrides what OSPF *believes* this link's MTU is — for the wire's
`DbdPacket.interface_mtu` field and DBD pagination sizing — independent
of the interface's real kernel MTU (mirrors real OSPF implementations'
`mtu-bytes`-style override). See `docs/protocols/ospf-internals.md`'s "LSA exchange and the LSDB".

mtu_ignore.description:
RFC 2328 §10.6: skip the Interface MTU check on a received DBD. By
default a neighbor advertising an MTU larger than this link's is
stuck in `ExStart`; set this to form the adjacency anyway.

name.description: Profile name, unique within its area.

oneOf.description:
`None` resolves per attach point: a `Subinterface`/loopback
`Interface` attach point defaults to `PointToPoint`, a
`BroadcastDomain` one defaults to `Broadcast` — resolved by
`ospf::reconcile`, not here, since one profile may be referenced by
attach points of different kinds at once. Setting this explicitly
overrides that default per attach point (e.g. forcing
point-to-point behavior on a `BroadcastDomain` attach point, or
vice versa) — never validated against the attach point's own kind,
matching real OSPF's own allowance for this.

priority.description:
`None` defaults to `PRIORITY_DEFAULT` (1). Governs RFC 2328 §9.4
DR/BDR election eligibility on a `Broadcast` attach point; sent on
the wire (but functionally inert) on a `PointToPoint` one too.

OspfVirtualLink.description:
One RFC 2328 §15 virtual link, configured on its transit area and keyed by
the far endpoint's router id. Timers and authentication are the link's own
(Appendix C.3), not a profile's: a virtual link has no attach point.

oneOf.description: `None` is `AuType` 0 (no authentication). Checked like a profile's.

dead_interval.description:
`None` defaults to 40s. Strictly greater than `hello_interval` when
both are set.

hello_interval.description: `None` defaults to 10s, as for a profile.

router_id.description: Router id of the far end of the virtual link; the key.

Ospfv3Area.description:
One `OSPFv3` area within an `Ospfv3Instance`, keyed by its dotted-quad area
id — mirrors `OspfArea` exactly. Unique only within its owning instance,
enforced on the parent's `areas` field (`ospfv3_instance::unique_area_ids`).

area_id.description: Area id in dotted-quad form; 0.0.0.0 is the backbone.

profiles.description: Interface profiles declared in this area, referenced by an interface's `ospfv3` attachment.

Ospfv3Instance.description:
A named `OSPFv3` (RFC 5340) instance — the IPv6 counterpart of
`OspfInstance`, kept as a fully parallel type rather than widened onto
it, since `OSPFv2` and `OSPFv3` are different wire protocols (different
packet/LSA formats) run by two independent daemons (`nos-ospfd`/
`nos-ospfv3d`) — see the `OSPFv3` Phase 1 plan. `router_id`/`area_id`
(on `Ospfv3Area`) stay `Ipv4Addr`: RFC 5340 keeps these as opaque 32-bit
identifiers, not real addresses, exactly like RFC 2328.

areas.description: This instance's `OSPFv3` areas, keyed by `area_id` — see `Ospfv3Area`.

extended_lsa.description:
RFC 8362 Full mode: originate/consume the TLV-based extended LSAs
(E-Router, E-Network, E-Link, E-Intra-Area-Prefix) instead of the
RFC 5340 legacy set. Off by default; `#[serde(default)]` so configs
saved before this field existed still load.

graceful_restart_grace_period.description:
RFC 5187 graceful restart: on a planned shutdown, send a Grace-LSA
asking every `Full` neighbor to keep the adjacency (and this router's
routes) for this many seconds while the daemon restarts. `None`
(default) disables it. Helper mode needs no config — every instance
always helps a restarting neighbor.

name.description: Instance name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among `OSPFv3` instances.

redistribute_policy.description:
The policy of the owning table's `redistribute … to ospfv3` rule,
mirrored like `OspfInstance.redistribute_policy` (derived, read-only).

router_id.description: 32-bit router id (RFC 5340 §2.1), written as an IPv4 dotted-quad.

routing_table.description:
The name of the `RoutingTable` that claims this instance (i.e. the
VRF it belongs to), mirrored from that table's `ospfv3_instance`
field — same derived/read-only pattern as `OspfInstance.routing_table`
(`crate::derive::sync_routing_table_refs`).

Ospfv3Profile.description:
A named `OSPFv3` profile, declared inside an area (`Ospfv3Area.profiles`)
but referenced by bare name from any L3 attach point's `ospfv3_profile`
field (`Interface`/`Subinterface`/`BroadcastDomain`) — mirrors
`OspfProfile` exactly, except that `auth` is RFC 7166's authentication
trailer (crypto only, no simple-password mechanism exists for `OSPFv3`),
so it's a bare key list rather than an `OspfAuth` enum. Reuses
`OspfProfile`'s `HELLO_INTERVAL_DEFAULT`/`DEAD_INTERVAL_DEFAULT`/
`PRIORITY_DEFAULT`/`NetworkType` directly — those defaults and the
point-to-point/broadcast distinction are unchanged by RFC 5340.

auth.description:
RFC 7166 authentication trailer keys; `None` means unauthenticated.
`key_id` is the 16-bit Security Association ID. HMAC-SHA only — RFC
7166 §4.3 defines no MD5 option. Same rotation model as
`OspfAuth::Crypto` (`is_current` signs, every key verifies).

bfd.description:
Name of a `BfdProfile` to run BFD with; `None` runs no BFD.
Inert until `nos-bfdd` exists.

cost.description: RFC 5340 §4.8 SPF metric. `None` defaults to `1`; `0` is rejected.

dead_interval.description:
`None` defaults to `OspfProfile::DEAD_INTERVAL_DEFAULT` (40s). When
both this and `hello_interval` are set, this must be strictly
greater — checked one level up on `Ospfv3Area.profiles`, mirroring
`ospf_profile::valid_profile_timers` exactly.

instance_id.description:
RFC 5340 §A.3.1 Instance ID (header byte 14) this profile's links send
and accept: a received packet carrying any other value is dropped.
`None` means 0. Limited to 0-31, RFC 5838 §2.1's IPv6-unicast range.

mtu.description:
`None` resolves to the attach point's own real interface MTU,
falling back to 1500 if unavailable — mirrors `OspfProfile.mtu`.

mtu_ignore.description:
RFC 2328 §10.6 (RFC 5340 §4.2.1): skip the Interface MTU check on a received DBD. By
default a neighbor advertising an MTU larger than this link's is
stuck in `ExStart`; set this to form the adjacency anyway.

name.description: Profile name, unique within its area.

oneOf.description: `None` resolves per attach point, exactly like `OspfProfile.network_type`.

priority.description:
`None` defaults to `1`. Governs RFC 5340 (via RFC 2328 §9.4) DR/BDR
election eligibility on a `Broadcast` attach point.

Pagination.description:
Pagination of a listing endpoint (#713; the convention #714 reuses): the
page size served and the cursor to pass back as `?after=`, `null` on the
last page. Keyset paging without a snapshot: a listing that changes
mid-walk never loops or repeats an item, but may miss or include a
concurrent change.

limit.description: The page size that applied (the requested `limit`, clamped).

next.description: Cursor of the next page, `null` on the last page.

PolicyDefinition.description:
A named RPL script (see `docs/architecture/rpl.md`), referenced by name from a `BgpPeerGroup`'s `import_policy`/
`export_policy`. Only the source text crosses the wire/IPC — each
consumer (`nos-bgpd`) compiles and caches its own bytecode locally,
matching the existing "each daemon re-resolves its own state from config
diffs" idiom, rather than `nos-proto` carrying a bytecode wire format.

name.description: Policy name, unique, and never the reserved `accept-all` or `deny-all`.

source.description: RPL source text, compiled at commit time and again by each consumer.

PortAggregate.description:
A named Linux bonding device, statically (`Xor`) or LACP-negotiated
(`Lacp`). Same
config surface as a *physical* `Interface` (never a loopback — bonding a
loopback makes no sense): `switching_profile`/`mtu`/`subinterfaces`, all
validated by the exact same helpers `Interface` uses, plus `mode`/
`lacp_rate`. All L3
config (addresses/routing-table/OSPF) lives under `subinterfaces` (tag 0
for the untagged/native case), exactly like a physical `Interface` — a
