`PortAggregate` never gets the loopback-style flat `addresses`/
`routing_table` fields, since there's no "loopback bond" concept. An
`Interface` becomes a bonded member by setting its own `port_aggregate`
field to this aggregate's name — the same reference-by-name shape
`Interface.switching_profile` already uses for L2 trunk membership —
rather than this type holding a member list itself.

acl_in.description:
Names an `Acl` filtering IP packets arriving on this bond; the placement
rules are `acl::valid_acl_references`.

acl_out.description: Names an `Acl` filtering IP packets leaving this bond.

bfd.description:
Name of a `BfdProfile`: runs one micro-BFD session (RFC 7130) per
member link, and a member is only enslaved while its session is Up.
Needs `bfd_peer`. `#[serde(default)]` so older configs still load.

bfd_peer.description:
The peer's L3 address the micro-BFD sessions are sent to (RFC 7130
uses the peer's address, not a link-local group). Must be of the
family of an address on this bond's tag-0 subinterface (the session
source). Ignored without `bfd`.

df_algorithm.description:
See [`DfAlgorithm`]. `#[serde(default)]` so a config persisted before
this field existed still loads (as modulo, what it always was).

esi.description:
The Ethernet Segment this bond attaches to (EVPN multi-homing, RFC
7432): ten colon-separated hex bytes. Set the same value on every PE
the customer device is dual-homed to. `nos-fdbd` puts it on the Type-2
routes for MACs learned on this bond and elects a Designated Forwarder
among the PEs that share it.

flowspec.description:
Applies the flowspec rules of the BGP instance owning this device's
routing table to the IP packets arriving here (RFC 8955 section 5:
ingress only); placement rules are `acl::valid_flowspec_placements`.

lacp_rate.description:
See [`LacpRate`]. `#[serde(default)]` so a config persisted before
this field existed still loads.

lacp_system_id.description:
Overrides `nos-lacpd`'s derived LACP Actor System ID for this bond, so
two PEs sharing an ESI can present the same actor to the customer
device. Only meaningful for a `Lacp`-mode aggregate.

lacp_system_priority.description:
The LACP Actor System Priority `nos-lacpd` advertises for this bond
(802.1AX); `None` = 32768. Lower is higher priority. Only meaningful
for a `Lacp`-mode aggregate; ignored (not rejected) otherwise.

min_links.description:
Minimum number of member ports that must be `Distributing` for the
bond to carry traffic: below it `nos-lacpd` pushes an empty active
set, so the kernel bond holds no member, while the ports keep
negotiating and the bond refills as soon as the count is met. 0 and 1
behave the same (any Distributing port is enough). Only meaningful
for a `Lacp`-mode aggregate; ignored (not rejected) otherwise, and not
checked against the member count, which lives on the `Interface`s.

mode.description: Static bond or LACP (802.1AX) with its negotiation parameters.

mtu.description: Bond MTU in bytes; `None` keeps the kernel default.

name.description: Bond name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among interfaces and aggregates.

redundancy_mode.description:
See [`EsRedundancy`]. `#[serde(default)]` so a config persisted before
this field existed still loads (as all-active, what it always was).

stp_port_profile.description:
Names an `StpPortProfile` for this bond as a spanning-tree port.
Inert until `nos-stpd`. An ESI aggregate needs one with
`edge-port admin` and `bpdu-guard` (see `valid_port_aggregates`).

subinterfaces.description:
This bond's own per-tag L3 attachment points — same type and same
tag-0-is-untagged/native convention as `Interface.subinterfaces`.

switching_profile.description:
Names a `SwitchingProfile` trunking this bond into one or more
`BroadcastDomain`s — same field, same meaning, as
`Interface.switching_profile`.

PortAggregateLacpSummary.description: One `PortAggregate`'s LACP engine state, for `show lacp [<name>]`.

actor_system_priority.description: The aggregate's advertised Actor System Priority.

min_links_met.description:
Whether enough ports are Distributing to meet `min_links`; `false`
means the bond was emptied even though ports may be negotiating.

PortAggregateMode.description:
How a `PortAggregate`'s member set is decided. Both variants create the
*same* underlying kernel bond device (`BondMode::BalanceXor` — see
`interface::driver::linux::bond_mode_of`'s doc comment for why `Lacp`
does **not** map to the kernel's own `Ieee8023Ad` bonding mode); the
difference is only which control plane decides which members are
actually enslaved into it.

PortAggregateStatus.description:
The wire twin of `schema::PortAggregate` — a static Linux bonding
device's config, the same shape as `InterfaceStatus` minus the
loopback-only flat `addresses`/`routing_table` fields (a bond is never a
loopback — all its L3 config lives in `subinterfaces`).

bond_name.description:
The real Linux bond device name the `linux` driver allocated for this
aggregate (e.g. `bond1`) — `None` until the driver has actually
created it (or under the `noop` driver, a synthesized placeholder).

err_disabled.description:
Observed: held administratively down by `nos-stpd`'s BPDU guard
(err-disabled). Read back by a restarting `nos-stpd`.

link_local_address.description:
See `InterfaceStatus.link_local_address` — same observed-kernel-state
semantics, scoped to this bond's own kernel device.

name.description: Name of the aggregate.

PrefixList.description:
A named set of prefix-match entries, referenced by bare name from an RPL
script's `this.prefix in NAME`.

entries.description: Entries, any of which may match.

name.description: List name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among prefix lists.

PrefixListEntry.description:
One `prefix-list` entry. `range: None` means exact match — this exact
prefix+length only; `Some((min, max))` means "contained within `cidr`,
with the candidate's own length in `[min, max]`". Deliberately different
from the existing `this.prefix in <cidr>` operator, which stays
containment/orlonger-based for a bare CIDR — see root `CLAUDE.md`'s RPL
section.

range.description: Prefix-length range `(min, max)` that matches within `cidr`; `None` is an exact match.

PrefixRoutes.description:
One prefix's full candidate list, ordered best (winner) to worst by
source preference.

candidates.description: All candidate routes for the prefix.

Redistribute.description:
`redistribute bgp`). The table holds a list keyed by `to`
`redistribute from static to bgp`). The table holds a list keyed by `to`
(at most one rule per target), so static routes can feed BGP, OSPF and
`OSPFv3` at once; an `Option<Redistribute>` from before the list is still
read from disk (`deserialize_redistribute`).

from.description: Protocol the redistributed routes come from.

metric.description:
OSPF external metric (1..=16777215) for the AS-external-LSAs this
rule originates; `None` = 20. Only valid with `to ospf`.

metric_type.description:
OSPF external metric type, 1 or 2 (RFC 2328 §16.4); `None` = 1. Only
valid with `to ospf`.

policy.description:
Names a `PolicyDefinition` (or the built-in `accept-all`/`deny-all`)
to filter redistributed routes through before they reach BGP.
Unlike `BgpPeerGroup.import_policy`/`export_policy`, `None` here
means **accept-all**, not `deny-all` — redistribution has no
filtering today, and defaulting to deny-all would silently break
every existing `redistribute from static to bgp` config.

to.description: Protocol receiving the routes; the key, so at most one rule per target.

RedistributeSource.description:
The source side of a `Redistribute` rule. Only `Static` exists today —
see `Redistribute`'s doc comment for why this is an enum rather than a
bare marker.

RedistributeTarget.description:
The target side of a `Redistribute` rule — `Bgp`, `Ospf` or `Ospfv3`. See
`Redistribute`'s doc comment.

ReflectorDiscards.description: Why the S-BFD reflector dropped a packet, counted per reason.

authenticated.description: The A bit is set: reflector authentication is not built yet.

malformed.description: Not a valid BFD Control packet.

rate_limited.description: Over the reflector's global packet rate.

unknown_discriminator.description: Your Discriminator is not one of the reflector's.

ReflectorView.description: The S-BFD reflector, for `show bfd reflector`.

discarded.description: Packets the S-BFD reflector discarded, by cause.

discriminators.description: The discriminators answered for, as 32-bit values.

RestApi.description:
Where `nos-restd` listens for a routing table: one specific address
inside the table's VRF. There is deliberately no wildcard — an
unauthenticated management API must be pinned to one reachable address.
Whether the address is actually configured on an interface in the VRF is
operational state, not validated at commit: `nos-restd` retries the bind.

address.description: Address the REST listener binds inside the VRF; no wildcard.

port.description: TCP port of the REST listener.

RouteEntry.description: One candidate route for a prefix.

backup.description:
Pre-computed backup next hop, installed in the kernel at a higher
metric so it takes over the instant the primary is withdrawn.

backup_tunnel.description:
`backup` is an RFC 7490 remote LFA: the PQ node the backup tunnels
(IP-in-IP) to, not a neighbor.

blackhole.description:
`discard` came from a BGP RFC 7999 blackhole (an OSPF ABR discard
stays `false`).

discard.description:
A discard (blackhole) route — no gateway; e.g. an OSPF ABR's route
for one of its advertised area ranges (RFC 2328 §3.5).

oneOf.description: Set on an `Evpn` candidate.

gateways.description:
Every next hop of this candidate — two or more is an equal-cost
multipath (ECMP) route, installed as one kernel route.

mpls_labels.description:
The MPLS label stack each of `gateways` is forwarded with (RFC 4364
section 4.3.4), outermost first, in `gateways` order; every stack is
empty for a source other than `Vpn`.

vpn.description:
The PE and RD each of `gateways` came from, in `gateways` order, on a
`Vpn` candidate; empty otherwise.

RouteSourceKind.description:
Wire twin of `nos-rib`'s internal `RouteSource` — kept separate so
`nos-rib`'s own domain type doesn't need to derive wire traits it has no
other use for.

items.description: Prefixes in ascending CIDR order, each with its candidates best to worst.

RoutingTable.description:
A named routing table, optionally associated with one BGP instance and
one static routing instance. The reference lives only on the table —
`BgpInstance`/`StaticRoutingInstance` have no notion of which table(s)
reference them.

bgp_instance.description: BGP instance bound to this table, if any.

evpn.description:
EVPN IP-VRF: this table's L3 VNI. `serde(default)` like `rest_api`.
`#[garde(skip)]`: checked by `valid_table_evpn` (it needs the other
tables and the broadcast domains).

name.description: Table name, 1 to 64 characters; also the VRF name.

ospf_instance.description: `OSPFv2` instance bound to this table, if any.

ospfv3_instance.description:
Same shape as `ospf_instance`, associating this table with an
`Ospfv3Instance` (RFC 5340) instead — a separate field, not a
widened `ospf_instance`, since `nos-ospfd`/`nos-ospfv3d` are two
independent daemons that can both legitimately claim the same table
(dual-stack OSPF on one VRF).

redistribute.description:
`#[garde(skip)]`: the cross-field constraint (the referenced
`bgp_instance`/`static_routing_instance` must actually be set on this
same table) can't live in a per-field closure — garde's per-field
`custom` closures can't see a sibling field — so it's wired one level
up, on `Config.routing_tables` (`valid_redistribute_rules`), the same
reason `BgpPeerGroup`'s timer check is wired on `BgpInstance.peer_groups`.

oneOf.description:
Pins a `nos-restd` to this table: it listens on `rest_api.address`
inside this table's VRF. `serde(default)` so on-disk config saved
before this field existed still loads.

static_routing_instance.description: Static routing instance bound to this table, if any.

vpn.description:
L3VPN identity (RD, route targets, underlay instance, label).
`serde(default)` like `evpn`; `#[garde(skip)]`: checked by
`valid_table_vpn` (it needs the other tables).

RoutingTableEvpn.description:
An IP-VRF's EVPN L3 VNI (RFC 9136 Type-5 routes, RFC 9135 symmetric
IRB in its "interface-less" form): `nos-ribd` creates `vx<l3_vni>` on a
bridge `brv<l3_vni>` in this table's VRF, originates every best route of
the table as a Type-5 into `bgp_instance` (the underlay instance, never
the table's own) and installs the Type-5 routes it receives back.

A plain struct with optional fields rather than an `Option<…>` (like
`Config.lldp`): the CLI then reaches every field on its own (`set
routing-table t evpn l3-vni 5000`, `… evpn route-target import <rt>`),
which an optional struct, set in one line, can't do for its lists.
Setting `l3_vni` turns it on; every other field requires it — see
`valid_table_evpn`.

bgp_instance.description: The underlay BGP instance the Type-5 routes are exchanged over.

l3_vni.description: The L3 VNI (1-16777215), unique across every table and broadcast domain.

rd.description: Route Distinguisher of every Type-5 route this table originates.

route_targets_export.description: Attached to every Type-5 route this table originates.

route_targets_import.description: A received Type-5 route must carry one of these to be installed.

oneOf.description:
The VTEP address, resolved at runtime by `nos-ribd`. `Loopback` is the
loopback of the routing table owning `bgp_instance`.

RoutingTableVpn.description:
A VRF's L3VPN identity (RFC 4364 VPNv4/VPNv6): the RD and route targets
of the routes this table exports into / imports from the VPN address
families of `bgp_instance` (the underlay instance, never the table's
own), plus an optional static MPLS label. Unset (all default) means the
table is not a VPN; any field requires the others, see `valid_table_vpn`.
No daemon consumes it yet (later sub-issues of #573).

bgp_instance.description: The underlay BGP instance the VPN routes are exchanged over.

label.description: Static MPLS label (16-1048575) for this VRF's exported routes.

rd.description: Route Distinguisher prepended to every exported prefix.

route_targets_export.description: Attached to every VPN route this table exports.

route_targets_import.description: A received VPN route must carry one of these to be imported.

site_of_origin.description:
Site of Origin (RFC 4364 section 7): attached to every route this
table exports; a received route carrying it is not imported here.

RpkiCache.description: One RPKI-to-Router cache (RFC 8210), keyed by its address.

address.description: Address of the RPKI-to-Router cache; the key.

oneOf.description:
RTR session authentication (RFC 8210 §9): TCP-MD5 or TCP-AO toward the
cache, same rules as `BgpPeerGroup.auth`. `None` is an unauthenticated
session. Keys are admin-keystore labels, like `BgpPeerGroup.auth`.
Appended last: postcard is positional.

port.description: TCP port of the cache, `RPKI_RTR_PORT_DEFAULT` unless set.

RpkiSessionState.description:
RFC 8210 session state of one configured RPKI cache, as seen by one
`nos-bgpd`.

RpkiValidationState.description: RFC 6811 origin validation state of a route, for `show bgp routes`.

SbfdReflector.description:
The S-BFD reflector: answers probes whose Your Discriminator is one of
`discriminators`, on UDP 7784 in every routing table's VRF. Off while the
list is empty. Keeps no per-initiator state.

allow_from.description:
RFC 7881 §7 source filtering: when not empty only probes from these
prefixes are answered. Empty accepts every non-martian source.

discriminators.description:
Each an S-BFD discriminator (RFC 7880 §4.1), written as an IPv4
address, the 32 bits of the value (`10.0.0.1` is 167772161).

SectionDiff.description:
A single named/keyed section (e.g. one BGP instance) that changed between
two configs, and the specific fields within it that did.

header.description:
Context line identifying the section, e.g. "bgp instance foo" —
always included even when `status` is `Modified` and the header
itself didn't change, so a reader can tell which section a changed
field belongs to without being shown the whole config.

name.description:
The section's identifying key as a plain string (e.g. a BGP
instance's `name`, a peer's `remote_address`, a route's `subnet`) —
structured, unlike `header`, so a machine consumer never has to parse
display text to find out which item changed.

status.description: Whether the object was added, removed or modified.

subsections.description:
Nested sections one level deeper (e.g. a BGP instance's peer-groups
and peers). Empty for a section with no nested collections.

SessionKey.description:
What identifies one BFD session: a routing table, the remote system and
the path to it (RFC 5881 single-hop is bound to an interface, RFC 5883
multihop is not).

aggregate.description:
RFC 7130 micro-BFD: the `PortAggregate` this session probes a member of
(`interface` is the member, `table` is empty). Appended last for postcard.

interface.description: Egress interface, required for single-hop sessions on link-local addresses.

multihop.description: Whether this is a multihop session (RFC 5883) rather than single-hop (RFC 5881).

table.description: Routing table (VRF) the session runs in.

reevaluated.description:
Per-family result of the local re-evaluation; absent when a
ROUTE-REFRESH was sent.

route_refresh.description:
`"sent"`: a ROUTE-REFRESH was delivered to the live session. `"none"`:
the peer-group keeps its received routes (soft reconfiguration
inbound), so the import policy was re-evaluated locally and nothing
was sent.

SourceAddress.description:
A peer-group's transport source address, referenced by interface + label
rather than a literal `IpAddr` — resolved to an actual address by
`nos-bgpd` at runtime (querying `nos-interfaced`, the same way a
`BgpInstance.routing_table` reference resolves to a VRF name via
`nos-ribd`), never here. `label` disambiguates which of an interface's
addresses to use when it carries more than one; `None` requires the
interface to carry exactly one address.

oneOf.description: An explicitly named interface.

interface.description: Interface whose address becomes the session's local address.

label.description: Selects one of the interface's addresses; `None` requires exactly one.

oneOf.description:
This peer-group's owning `BgpInstance`'s own loopback interface
(`loopback-<table>`, where `<table>` is that instance's
`routing_table`) — so no interface name needs to be spelled out.
Invalid (an error, not a fallback) for an instance with no owning
routing table, exactly like `BgpInstance.routing_table` itself.

Loopback.description:
This peer-group's owning `BgpInstance`'s own loopback interface
(`loopback-<table>`, where `<table>` is that instance's
`routing_table`) — so no interface name needs to be spelled out.
Invalid (an error, not a fallback) for an instance with no owning
routing table, exactly like `BgpInstance.routing_table` itself.

label.description: Selects one of the loopback's addresses; `None` requires exactly one.

SpanningTree.description: Bridge-wide spanning-tree parameters; there is exactly one per device.

oneOf.description: Protocol version forced on every port; `None` negotiates.

max_hops.description: MSTP hop budget of a BPDU, 6..=40.

mst_instances.description: MST instances and this bridge's priority in each.

tx_hold_count.description: BPDUs a port may send per second, 1..=10.

StaticRoute.description:
A single static route within a `StaticRoutingInstance`.

Known simplification: exactly one gateway per subnet is supported — ECMP
(multiple gateways for one subnet) is not modeled in this iteration.
Per-instance uniqueness of `subnet` is enforced on the *parent's*
`routes` field (`static_routing_instance::unique_subnets`), not here — a
`StaticRoute` in isolation has no notion of which instance owns it under
garde's whole-`Config` validation context.

bfd.description:
Name of a `BfdProfile` to run BFD with; `None` runs no BFD.
Inert until `nos-bfdd` exists.

gateway.description: Next-hop address, in the same family as `subnet`.

subnet.description: Destination prefix; the key within the instance.

StaticRoutingInstance.description:
A named container of static routes. Carries no reference to any routing
table — only `RoutingTable.static_routing_instance` names it, never the
other way around.

name.description: Instance name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among static routing instances.

routes.description: Routes of this instance, keyed by destination prefix.

StpCounterRow.description:
One row of `GET /v1/spanning-tree/counters`: a port's RFC 4318 counters
in one tree. Outside Rapid-PVST+ the counters belong to the port (the
CIST and every MSTI share them), so `tree` is `cist`.

tree.description: `cist`, or the broadcast domain's name in `mode rapid-pvst`.

StpForceVersion.description: Compatibility mode forced on every port (802.1Q 13.7 `ForceProtocolVersion`).

StpInstance.description: One tree of an MST region: instance 0 is the CIST.

domains.description: The broadcast domains running in this instance.

root_path_cost.description: Cost of the path to the root.

root_port.description: `None` when this bridge is the root of the instance.

vlans.description:
The VIDs mapped to this instance (`10,20-30`), derived from the
broadcast domains' tags.

StpInstancePort.description: One port in one spanning-tree instance of an MST region (#321).

boundary.description: The peer is outside the region: the instance follows the CIST here.

compat.description: Rapid-PVST+: the port talks 802.1D (PVST+) to its peer in this tree (#322).

designated_bridge.description: Designated Bridge ID on the segment.

designated_port.description: Designated Port ID on the segment.

inconsistent.description:
Rapid-PVST+: a BPDU named another VLAN than this tree's (PVID
inconsistency); the port is blocked in this tree (#322).

name.description: Port name.

state.description:
The state the kernel is given for this tree's domains (a boundary
port's is the CIST's).

StpMst.description: The MST region and its trees (`mode mstp`).

digest.description: The MST configuration digest, 32 hex digits.

instances.description: Instance 0 (the CIST) first, then every configured MSTI.

StpPortCounters.description:
Per-port BPDU and event counters, named after RFC 4318 (`dot1dStpPort*`).
They count since the bridge was last (re)built; in `mode mstp` the MSTIs
share the CIST's counters (one BPDU carries them all).

protocol_migration.description: Times the port switched between 802.1D and RSTP.

tc_received.description: BPDUs received with the topology-change flag, and TCN BPDUs.

tc_sent.description: BPDUs sent with the topology-change flag, and TCN BPDUs.

StpPortInfo.description:
One spanning-tree port. Bridge and port ids are display strings
(`8000.02:aa:bb:cc:dd:ee`, `128.1`), as `LldpNeighbor` does.

bpdu_guard.description: The protections configured on the port (`stp-port-profile`, #320).

cost.description: Path cost this port adds to the root path.

designated_bridge.description: The designated bridge/port on this port's segment.

designated_port.description: Designated Port ID on the segment.

edge.description: `operEdge`: the port is an edge port right now.

err_disabled.description: BPDU guard took the port down.

err_recovery_secs.description: Seconds until an `err_disabled` port recovers; `None`: manual `clear`.

loop_inconsistent.description: Loop guard holds the port in Discarding: BPDUs stopped arriving.

name.description: Port name.

root_inconsistent.description: Root guard holds the port in Discarding: a superior BPDU keeps arriving.

StpPortMstInstance.description:
This port's cost and priority in one MST instance, which must exist in
`spanning-tree mst-instance`.

cost.description: Administrative path cost in this instance; `None` derives it from link speed.

priority.description: Port priority in this instance, a multiple of 16.

StpPortProfile.description: Per-port spanning-tree settings that a switching profile attaches to ports.

bpdu_filter.description: Neither send nor process BPDUs on this port.

bpdu_guard.description: Shut the port (`err-disabled`) when a BPDU arrives on it.

bpdu_guard_recovery.description: Seconds before an `err-disabled` port comes back; `None`: never.

cost.description: `None`: automatic from the link speed (802.1Q Table 13-4).

link_type.description: Link type that governs the rapid transitions.

loop_guard.description: Block the port when BPDUs stop arriving instead of forwarding.

name.description: Profile name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among port profiles.

restricted_tcn.description:
Do not propagate topology changes received on this port (802.1Q
`restrictedTcn`).

root_guard.description: Never let this port become the root port.

StpRegion.description:
The MST region identity (802.1Q 13.8): bridges only share an MSTI tree
when name and revision match.

name.description: Region name; bridges join one region only when name and revision match.

StpState.description: The port state as the core sees it (the kernel's `Blocking` is `Discarding`).

StpSummary.description:
`show spanning-tree`. `enabled: false` (mode neither `rstp` nor `mstp`)
leaves the rest at its default.

Fields are only ever appended.

oneOf.description: The MST region and its trees; `None` outside `mode mstp` (#321).

pvst.description:
One tree per broadcast domain in `mode rapid-pvst` (#322); `id` is the
domain's VLAN. Empty in the other modes.

root_path_cost.description: Cost of the path to the root.

root_port.description: `None` when this bridge is the root.

oneOf.description: Cause of the most recent topology change.

last_port.description: The port the last change came in on, or started at.

last_secs_ago.description: Seconds since the last change; `None` before the first.

Subinterface.description:
One VLAN-scoped L3 attachment point on a physical `Interface`. `tag == 0`
is the untagged/native case — what used to be `Interface.addresses`/
`routing_table` directly, before L3 config moved under per-tag
subinterfaces. `1..=4094` is a real 802.1q tag, realized by
`nos-interfaced`'s Linux driver as its own `<interface>.<tag>` kernel
sub-interface (the same convention already used for a `Dot1q`
switching-profile member). A tag used by a `Subinterface` here and a tag
used by the same interface's `switching_profile` (an `Untagged` member
claims tag 0, a `Dot1q(n)` member claims tag `n`) must be disjoint — see
`valid_subinterface_and_switching_profile_tags`. Loopback interfaces
never have any `Subinterface`s — see `valid_addressing_split`.

acl_in.description:
Names an `Acl` filtering IP packets arriving on this subinterface; the
placement rules are `acl::valid_acl_references`.

acl_out.description: Names an `Acl` filtering IP packets leaving this subinterface.

addresses.description: Addresses on this subinterface, no duplicates.

bfd_unsolicited.description:
RFC 9468: names a `BfdProfile` for the passive sessions created by
unsolicited BFD Control packets (Your Discriminator 0) on this
subinterface. Requires `routing_table` on the same subinterface: the
VRF decides the socket.

flowspec.description:
Applies the flowspec rules of the BGP instance owning this device's
routing table to the IP packets arriving here (RFC 8955 section 5:
ingress only); placement rules are `acl::valid_flowspec_placements`.

mtu.description:
Overrides the MTU of this VLAN sub-link, in bytes. `None` follows the
parent's MTU. Must not exceed the parent's effective MTU and is
rejected on tag 0 (the physical link itself) — see
`valid_subinterface_mtus`.

ospf_profile.description:
If set, names an `OspfProfile` this subinterface joins OSPF under.
Requires `routing_table` also set on this same subinterface — OSPF
has no meaning without an L3/VRF context, see
`valid_subinterface_ospf_profile_requires_routing_table`.

ospfv3_profile.description:
Same shape as `ospf_profile`, joining `OSPFv3` (RFC 5340) instead — a
separate field, not a widened `ospf_profile`, so one subinterface can
run v2 and v3 simultaneously (real dual-stack routers do this
routinely). Also requires `routing_table` set on this same
subinterface — see `valid_subinterface_ospf_profile_requires_routing_table`.

routing_table.description: Routing table (VRF) the subinterface joins, if any.

tag.description: 802.1Q VLAN id of the subinterface; 0 is the untagged attachment.

SubinterfaceStatus.description:
The wire twin of `schema::Subinterface` — one VLAN-scoped L3 attachment
point on a physical interface, `tag == 0` for the untagged/native case.

link_local_address.description:
See `InterfaceStatus.link_local_address` — same observed-kernel-state
semantics, scoped to this subinterface's own kernel device.

mtu.description:
Effective MTU of this sub-link: its own override if configured, else
the parent's `mtu`. Desired config, like `InterfaceStatus.mtu`.

routing_table.description: Routing table (VRF) the object is enslaved to, if any.

SwitchingProfile.description:
A named, trunk-style container mapping multiple broadcast domains to
their dot1q tagging. Will be assigned to a future "switched interface"
config object — not modeled yet.

members.description: Broadcast domains a port using this profile carries.

name.description: Profile name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among switching profiles.

SwitchingProfileMember.description:
One broadcast domain's membership in a `SwitchingProfile`, tagged as
either a specific dot1q VLAN or untagged.

broadcast_domain.description: Name of the member `BroadcastDomain`; the key.

stp_cost.description:
Spanning-tree port cost for the ports using this membership; `None`:
the profile's or automatic. Inert until `nos-stpd`.

stp_priority.description: Spanning-tree port priority for this membership; a multiple of 16.

tag.description: How the member's frames are tagged on the port.

SyslogFacility.description:
The user-level facilities, `local0`-`local7`; the others are reserved for
operating-system subsystems.

address.description:
The collector's address. An IP, not a name: there is no resolver
inside a VRF.

oneOf.description: Syslog facility of every message. Default `local7`.
Minimum severity exported. Default `info`.

name.description: Collector name, unique among syslog servers.

routing_table.description: Send from inside this routing table's VRF. Default: the default netns.

oneOf.description:
How the collector is authenticated; required by (and only valid with)
transport `tls`. There is no "trust anything" mode.

transport.description:
Transport. Default `udp` (RFC 5426); `tcp` uses RFC 6587 octet counting;
`tls` is RFC 5425 over post-quantum TLS 1.3 and needs a `tls` block.

SyslogTls.description:
Authentication of a TLS syslog collector (RFC 5425 §4.2). Server
authentication only: `nos-logd` presents no client certificate.

allow_tls12.description:
Also allows TLS 1.2 with classical (non-post-quantum) key exchange, for
collectors that need RFC 9662; TLS 1.3 stays post-quantum only, but
traffic sent over TLS 1.2 can be decrypted by a future quantum computer.

fingerprint.description:
`SHA-256:AB:CD:...`: the SHA-256 of the collector's own certificate
(RFC 5425 §4.2.2). Exactly one of this and `trust_anchor`.

server_name.description:
The DNS name the collector's certificate must carry. Default: match the
collector's address against the certificate's IP address SANs.

trust_anchor.description:
PEM CA certificate(s) the collector's certificate must chain to
(RFC 5425 §4.2.1). Exactly one of this and `fingerprint`.

SyslogTransport.description: How a syslog server is reached.

TransactionSnapshot.description:
A named transaction's current state, returned after `OpenTransaction`,
`ApplyOp`, and `GetTransaction`.

dirty.description:
True once any `ApplyOp` has succeeded since the transaction was
(re)created.

generation.description:
Monotonic per-transaction edit counter: 0 when created, +1 on every
successful `ApplyOp`/`SetTransactionPath`. The value an `if_match`
precondition (and `nos-restd`'s `ETag`) compares against.

name.description: Name of the config.

resumed.description:
True if `OpenTransaction` attached to a pre-existing transaction
rather than creating a new one.

User.description:
A local user who may log in to `nos-cli` and call the REST API (HTTP
Basic). Every user is a full administrator — there are no roles.

name.description: Login name, 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, `_`, `-`), unique among users.

password.description:
An argon2id hash at rest. Setting a clear-text value is allowed — the
config daemon replaces it with a hash (keeping the old hash when the
clear text still matches it, so re-setting the same password is not a
change).

items.description: One instance's answer to a router-wide query: its payload, or why it has none.

VlanTag.description:
A dot1q tag, or the absence of one. `Dot1q`'s value is restricted to
`1..=4094` — 802.1Q reserves 0 and 4095.

oneOf.description: Frames carry no VLAN tag.
Frames carry this 802.1Q tag, 1 to 4094.

VpnRouteInfo.description:
Where a `Vpn`-sourced candidate came from: the remote PE (the BGP next
hop, resolved in the underlay into the candidate's gateway) and the
Route Distinguisher it was received under.

pe_next_hop.description: The remote PE: the VPN route's BGP next hop.

VpnRouteSummary.description:
One received VPN-IPv4/VPN-IPv6 path (RFC 4364/4659, SAFI 128), for
`show bgp vpnv4|vpnv6`. RD and Route Targets are rendered by `nos-bgpd`.

best.description: This path is the best one for its (RD, prefix), the one reflected.

labels.description: The MPLS label stack as received (RFC 8277), outermost first.

next_hop.description: The BGP next hop (the egress PE).

site_of_origin.description: The Site of Origin the path carries (RFC 4364 section 7), `65001:77`.

mtls.description: A client certificate issued by POST /v1/login (or /v1/renew)

info.description: Every `show` query and the transaction/config editing surface of the NOS shell. Every request needs a TLS client certificate: `POST /v1/login` (the only route without one) trades the password of a user in the config (`set user <name> password <clear>`) for a certificate, and every later request presents it in the handshake — no credentials are sent again. The connection is TLS 1.3 with post-quantum key exchange (X25519MLKEM768) only, and speaks HTTP/2 so many requests share one connection. The config tree is the URL tree — `/v1/transactions/{tx}` is the whole in-progress config and each path below it a subsection; `diff` and `commit` are reserved.

domain's VXLAN bridge port, so the bridge answers an ARP request or

Type-2 carrying an IP is installed as one) instead of flooding it
over the fabric. Gratuitous ARP is then no longer flooded to the
VXLAN port either. Off by default; requires a `vni`.

schema.description:

VRF it belongs to), mirrored from that table's `ospf_instance` field.
Derived and read-only: never set by any `OspfInstanceOp`, recomputed
by `nos-config` (`crate::derive::sync_routing_table_refs`) on every
commit and on load, so an operator only ever edits the one
authoritative reference (`RoutingTable.ospf_instance`). `nos-ospfd`
reads this directly to resolve its own VRF without scanning every
routing table. Deliberately not rendered by `nos-cli`.

schema.description:
Minimum number of member ports that must be `Distributing` for the
bond to carry traffic: below it `nos-lacpd` pushes an empty active
set, so the kernel bond holds no member, while the ports keep
negotiating and the bond refills as soon as the count is met. 0 and 1
behave the same (any Distributing port is enough). Only meaningful
for a `Lacp`-mode aggregate; ignored (not rejected) otherwise, and not
checked against the member count, which lives on the `Interface`s.

Names a `PolicyDefinition` (or the built-in `accept-all`/`deny-all`)
to filter redistributed routes through before they reach BGP.
Unlike `BgpPeerGroup.import_policy`/`export_policy`, `None` here
means **accept-all**, not `deny-all` — redistribution has no
filtering today, and defaulting to deny-all would silently break
every existing `redistribute from static to bgp` config.
